"Honestly, Mills. Today was great, better than great. It reminded me of how we used to be like this damn near every day before you left. I hate it to think it'll be even longer before we see each other again."
―Sallie May to Millie
Sallie May[6] is Millie's younger[2] sister and one of the two daughters of Lin and Joe. She lives with her parents alongside her three unnamed brothers and helps out in the Rough n' Tumbleweed Ranch.

She is a minor character who made her debut in "The Harvest Moon Festival".

Appearance

Sallie May is a rather tall imp, roughly the same height as Blitzo, with light maroon skin and a pair of serrated, black-and-white-striped horns atop her head. Her eyes sport yellow sclera, slit-like pupils, and long eyelashes protruding from them, with a single white scar over her right eye and on her notched eyebrow.

Her charcoal-colored hair is long with white-colored roots, and is usually tied back into a ponytail by a brown hair tie with messy bangs that covers her left eye. Tied around the back of her head is a red bandana with holes.

Her attire consists of a sleeveless, black turtleneck crop-top with various tears at the bottom, heavily ripped black leggings under a set of gray-beige short-shorts held by a black belt with an oval-shaped dark gray buckle, and matching-colored cowboy ankle boots.
Personality

Sallie May is shown to be just as cheerful and violent as her sister. She is also shown to be relatively snarky, most notably towards Moxxie.

According to herself, Sallie May is more careful to hide the bodies of people she's killed, unlike Millie. She also appears to be a bit more laid-back than Millie, as shown from the way she talks.

In "Hell's Belles", she reveals that she misses her sister and is sad that she never visits home often because of her life in Imp City, making her have to help her parents out with everything in Millie's place. She slowly begins to overcome this when Millie says that she will never be too busy for her sister and that, since their brothers are older and able to help their parents at the ranch, she can visit too.

Similarly to Millie, she doesn't like being hit on by strangers, especially if she's not interested in them.
Abilities

Athleticism - Similarly to her sister Millie, she has great athletic prowess.
Skillset

Weapon-handling - While she hasn't wielded any real weapons on-screen yet, she is very proficient in wielding even a fake weapon, such as a fake chainsaw on a VR arcade game.
Stealth - Sallie May seems to be good with stealth, as she is able to hide dead bodies without anyone suspecting her having a neighborhood head count.
Trivia

According to Morgana Ignis, "Sallie May" is the character's full first name.[6]
In a Twitter post, Morgana Ignis confirmed Sallie May is a transgender woman,[7] which was subsequently confirmed by the Helluva Boss Twitter as well.[8]
This is also implied in her design, as her horns have thick white stripes, which is a trait only seen on the horns of biological male imps.
She also has white roots on her otherwise black hair; white hair is a common trait among biological male imps while biological females have black hair, showing she dyed it to pass better.
According to Morgana Ignis, Sallie May being transgender was always the plan, even way before they began designs.[9] Morgana also explains that because Millie's sister was planned to be transgender, Vivziepop definitely wanted a transgender actress and had Morgana in mind for her, with voicing Sallie May being a direct offer from Vivziepop.[10]
In an Instagram post, Morgana confirmed that Sallie May's lesbian sexuality will be confirmed in the show.[11]
Like Sallie May, Morgana Ignis is also a transgender lesbian woman.[11][12]
According to Morgana Ignis there are a ton of plans for Sallie May, many of which having already been written and recorded.[9] This may imply that Sallie May will return beyond the second season, as Vivian Nixon previously said that season two had already been recorded in 2022.[13]
According to Morgana, Sallie May and Millie have a lot more stories to be told, and their interaction in "The Harvest Moon Festival" wasn't accurate to what their relationship is actually like.[14]
Morgana mentioned that Sallie May's time for an entire episode will come and there will be stories involving her.[15]
For the "Hell's Belles" short, Morgana felt that if she was going to the city, she wanted to give Sallie a new look that worked a little more for the city because Sallie May's normal outfit in Wrath is her work clothes, logically like how the members of I.M.P got new outfits in the Wrath Ring for "The Harvest Moon Festival".[16]
She shares the same voice actor as the Catfish Monster, with both of them being voiced by Morgana Ignis.
According to Sterling Richter, Ignis requested that Sallie May have a visible bulge in the sexually-oriented parts of merchandise because many transgender females don't tuck all the time, but the original merchandise designs were more cisgender in sex appeal.[17]
Morgana explained that when making the merch, Morgana was consulted with and asked if there should be any changes made. As the initial design for it had a much more flat crotch area like the other female characters, Morgana advocated to show that there is no shame with not hiding that part of the body. Likewise, she wanted to present Sallie May's feelings about her body in a positive light without hiding her transgender identity.[18]

entries.content:
NAME
Sinner Demons
LOCATION

"I don't think there's anything left that could save such loathsome sinners! The chance given was the life they lived before, the punishment is this! There is no undoing what is done!"
―Alastor, to Charlie about the idea of redemption
Sinner Demons, also known simply as Sinners, are a subspecies of demons that were all once humans who committed sins or crimes before they died, which results in them being damned to Hell as their punishment in the afterlife.[1]

They are ranked above Hellborn demons such as Succubi, Imps, and Hellhounds in terms of Hell's hierarchy.


ADVERTISEMENT
Description


1/2


Martha as a human
Martha as a human
Martha as a sinner
Martha as a sinner
Sinners are a large group of demons whose appearance and abilities vary widely due to their demonic forms corresponding to their human self's aspects. They are in the lower-middle levels of Hell's hierarchy, above the three lowest tiers.[2] Sinners have known limitations that separate them from the natural Hellborn demons; for instance, all Sinners are confined to the Pride Ring and are unable to traverse through the other rings.[3]

Furthermore, Sinners are the only known species of demon that cannot reproduce, which is part of their punishment, but can still have sex.[4] Although they are the souls of dead humans, these demons are shown to still consume food and the like, which suggests that their bodies still need the intake in order to survive. They also apparently need to sleep.

Despite these setbacks, Sinners have the rare privilege of changing their social status by gaining additional power, either by making deals with stronger demons and/or taking power by force.[5] Those who have accumulated enough power through these deals can rise in social status[6] and rise to the next class in the hierarchy, the Overlords. Furthermore, sinners are ageless and do not physically age and, therefore, will not die from the natural passage of time. Nonetheless, they can still be hurt, and in certain conditions, killed.

Additionally, some Sinners can enter a state of partialism, where elements of their full demonic form make their way into their humanoid form. This seems to be voluntary, occurring if they feel sinister or when they feel strong emotions such as anger.
Cultural Relations

Within the populaces of Heaven and Hell, there has been bias and stigma towards Sinners, mainly from Angels, as Sinners had their chance to do what is right on Earth but went to Hell because they committed unforgivable acts which earned them eternal damnation. With this, many angels and demons refuse to give another thought about Sinners and view them as irredeemable, and some deny that Sinners should get a second chance to enter Heaven under the belief that divine judgement is unquestionable and is final at death. Many Sinners actually adopt this view, believing they blew their one shot into Heaven and as such don't want to try redeem themselves. For instance, when several Sinners hear Charlie's announcement of the Happy Hotel, they laughed at and mock the idea, and Alastor, whilst being a Sinner working with the Hotel, doesn't believe Sinners can change for the better, calling them "loathsome", and aware that they can't undo what is done. Similarly, Valentino mocks the idea that Angel Dust can improve.

Lucifer in particular, a fallen angel himself, downright admits Sinners are horrible thanks to abusing the gift of free will he and Lilith gave them, and even made sure only Sinners would die during the Extermination, while the Hellborn are pardoned. The Exorcists, Adam and Lute, refuse to believe Sinners should be given a chance at redemption, and are willing to punish any Exorcist who dares to spare even one from death. Vaggie, while having abandoned her Exorcist life and views, is still wary of Sinners who could hurt her or Charlie. Despite this, several Angels in Heaven's courthouse, including the Seraphim Emily, were horrified that Sinners were being killed annually, and that Sera, the High Seraphim, allowed this.

Some Hellborn also have a low opinion of Sinners, with some such contempt seeming to stem from the Sinners' human roots, with Millie believing humans to be inherently vile and them being sentenced to Hell as evidence behind the callous predisposition a Sinner expresses. However, the majority of Hellborns have little to no problem living and working beside Sinners within the Pride Ring.

Biology

Appearance

There is no true extent to a Sinner's appearance, since it is the manifestation of the soul in question. Usually, a human's demon form is influenced by the human's soul, sins or crimes.[7][8][9] An example being Angel Dust and his family: since he was in the mafia, he and his family members who are with him in Hell have spider-like appearances because of their "web" of crimes.[10] Sometimes, the form is influenced by the human's death, such as Lyle Lipton acquiring teeth akin to that of piano keys after being crushed to death by a falling piano.

In general, their standard appearance is humanoid, in the sense of having humanoid body structure: being bipedal (with a few exceptions, such as Lyle Lipton and Sir Pentious, that have no legs), possessing opposable thumbs and having an upright posture.

Abilities

Most, if not all, Sinners share the following traits:

Demon transformation - A few Sinners have demonstrated the ability to transform into larger, stronger, and more demonic alternate forms, as shown by Alastor and Killjoy.
Animalistic tendencies - When a Sinner has an animal theme, the Sinner will have certain behaviors related to it. Alastor, a deer-themed sinner, makes elk bugle noises when entering his full demon form and bleats like a fawn if he's feeling contentment. Valentino, a moth-themed sinner, makes squeaking noises every now and then. Husk, a cat-like sinner, purrs if feeling contentment.
Immortality - Sinners do not age and remain the same age as when they died (ex: Alastor died in his 30s, so he will remain in his 30s forever in Hell), and thus do not die of old age and other natural causes that kill humans. They also cannot die via damage to the body or from earth-borne illnesses. When a Sinner is damaged or hurt in an extreme way (ex: being crushed by a piece of rubble), they will not die from it.[11] It has yet to be shown how the Sinner recovers; however, "Radio Killed the Video Star" has Velvette imply that, if a Sinner is completely dismembered, even by another Sinner as powerful as an Overlord, they may slowly "pull themselves back together" after some time. However, Sinners can still be killed once they are hit with any Angelic Weapons.[12][13]
Superhuman durability - Since Sinners are already the dead souls of humans, they are highly resilient and are unharmed by most things that can harm humans. However, there are things that can injure or incapacitate a demon, Sinner or Hellborn, that being infected by Hell's own diseases and the like,[14][15] or if a demon is struck by an Angelic weapon.[16]
Drug and alcohol tolerance - As Sinners are already "dead", they're free to indulge in drug addiction and alcoholism as they can't die from a drug overdose or alcohol poisoning.
Unique abilities - Whereas Hellborn Demons have specific powers attributed to their species, Sinners are offered a larger selection of abilities that varies by individual. These range from Alastor's wide arsenal of powers, Angel's additional sets of arms, or Husk's ability to fly.
Mortality

Sinners can only be killed by angelic weapons; these are made from a special metal and are typically wielded by Exorcists.[12]

When Sinners are fatally hit by an angelic weapon, it results in the "erasure" or "final death" of the demon,[12] and the demon's body is "killed off", while the remaining dark energy in the soul is left to wander into inanimate objects in its surroundings, which explains why some things such as regular furniture have functioning eyes.[17] However, if they are simply injured by an angelic weapon, they can survive but will take time to recover.

However, in the case of Sir Pentious in "The Show Must Go On", Adam vaporized him with angelic light, possibly implying that a Sinner can be killed with angelic magic. Although, it is unknown if it can permanently kill a Sinner like an angelic weapon since Sir Pentious ascended into Heaven as a redeemed soul.

Redemption

A rare and esoteric phenomenon, redemption is when a Sinner can ascend to Heaven and become an Angel. Because of the rarity of this event, as well as lack of information on what causes redemption, the details of this process and requirements of how to do so are not defined. Furthermore, as Sinners express an overall disinterest in attempting to change their ways, most demons and angels view the chance of redemption as impossible.

The only known case of redemption occurring is with Sir Pentious; following him proclaiming his love for Cherri Bomb, he attacked Adam from his blimp as an act of self-sacrifice. After being immediately vaporized by Adam, he was sent to Heaven and became the first Sinner to be redeemed. This may suggest that in order to be redeemed, one has to resolve to be a better person and act selfless. However, it is unknown if the act of a "selfless sacrifice" is necessary or required to achieve this.

ADVERTISEMENT

Trivia

They are one of two non-Hellborn species of demon, the other being fallen angels, which are Heavenborn.
Sinners are the only species of Earthborn demon. They are also the only demons that Exorcists are allowed to kill, as Hellborn species have been pardoned.
The creature that each Sinner is turned into when they become demons are associated with their human life, or as Vivziepop puts it, individual reflections of their souls.[8] Because of this, their appearances are actually not randomized as many fans have speculated.
In some cases, the form sinners take reflects the way in which they died, such as the camp counselor shown in "Unhappy Campers" taking on an aquatic appearance due to his death from drowning in a lake (a similar case also applies to Baxter), or Lyle Lipton's demon form having teeth resembling piano keys after being crushed by a grand piano.
When Sinners arrive at Hell, they make up their own name that they are known for as demons. However, Alastor did not since he dislikes giving himself any sort of nickname.[18]
This also holds true for business partners, Loopty Goopty and Lyle Lipton.
Since demons theoretically cannot die via natural causes, such as Earth-based illnesses and overdosing, Sinners are able to consume amounts that would be lethal to humans without any risk of dying.
This is shown in both Angel Dust and Husk, as both are able to consume vast amounts of drugs and alcohol without any threat of death.
In "C.H.E.R.U.B", Blitzo was able to figure out that Loopty had just been sent to Hell recently judging by his scent from Earth, implying that Sinners retain their smell from the living world but it may eventually fade away.
Because Sinners are technically already dead, they usually refer to their time on Earth as being "alive" and their time in Hell as their "afterlife".
Sinners are the only species of demon to be considered "dead", as Hellborn demons can age and die through natural causes.
In a development stream, artist Faustisse stated that demons can transform when enraged or when in combat.[note 1] In the series, while several Sinners have demonstrated this ability, it is unknown if this is an ability all Sinners possess or is specific to certain individuals.
According to Faustisse, Sinners have alternate forms if ever they were sent to Heaven.[note 2] However, it is unknown if this referred to humans who died and became angels instead of demons, or humans that already became Sinners.
The latter is the case with Sir Pentious when is sent to Heaven he gained a new form that is similar but different from that of his demon self.
According to Vaggie in "Radio Killed the Video Star", Sinners are said to be desperate, and that they may be desperate enough to try anything to escape the extermination, indicating that Sinners might leave themselves open to any sort of danger and vulnerability to ensure their survival such as choosing to give up their soul in a deal to an Overlord.
It is unknown how a Sinner arrives in Hell after they die on Earth and are damned to Hell. During the show's production, Vivziepop noted that while the process was still in development, she did confirm that where a human died on Earth is where they will arrive in Hell.[19]
According to Faustisse, a human's voice changes when they are transformed into Sinner demons, possibly into whatever fits proper.[note 3]
This detail may have been retconned as it is not the case with Mrs. Mayberry onwards, since she and the other Sinners retained their human voices even after they went to Hell. However, when Alastor arrived in Hell, his voice switches between his normal human voice to having a radio filter.
Sinners retain and keep their memories from when they were alive, even memory of how they died.
Sinners do not have powers when they first show up in Hell, instead they gain their powers by "leveling up" over time.[20] However, this may not always be the case, as in the pilot episode, Vaggie explained that when Alastor first arrived in Hell, he possessed raw power that had never been harnessed by a human soul before, indicating that there are rare cases for a Sinner to have powers upon their arrival.

―Stella, to Stolas
Stella is Stolas' wife, Octavia's mother, and a supporting antagonist in Helluva Boss who made her debut in the Helluva Boss pilot.

She has hired an assailant, who is actively tracking down the former's husband, but she is stopped by her brother after being convinced that having Stolas alive is of much more worth to them than having him dead.


ADVERTISEMENT
Appearance


2/2




Main Series

Stella is a tall, slim, white avian demon. Stella has long, hair-like feathers that have gray tips and a large gray stripe on her head. She has a short pink beak, and very long curved eyelashes.

She has gray markings underneath her eyes, which themselves have red sclera with light pupils.

For attire, Stella wears a white dress with puffed sleeves and feather trimming, along with black accents. She is seen wearing a crown, and has painted nails underneath her black gloves.

Pilot

In the pilot, Stella's overall look was significantly different. She had a much lankier figure and feathers consisting of shades of green and pale yellow, and her eyes had green irises with black pupils. Her beak was not present, presumably being covered by her feathers.

Moreover, Stella wore a green and white dress, with white and red gloves. The only element that appears unchanged in both designs is her crown.

ADVERTISEMENT

Personality

Stella seems to be very temperamental about her husband's infidelity to the point of verbally and almost physically attacking him while screaming, breaking a lot of possessions and even assaulting an imp butler.

However, she seems to be more baffled by said infidelity specifically happening with an imp, a demon of lower position; she is also incensed that Stolas spoke of his inability to go to a motel to consummate it. Given Octavia's indifferent attitude towards her aggressive outburst, it can be assumed Stella has these outbursts on a frequent basis.

Given her choice of words during her argument with Stolas, it seems she is very classist, as she is not only furious at his infidelity but also at his debasement in position, choice of lovers and actions, since she berated him for acting like a plebeian.

In fact, it's shown, in "The Harvest Moon Festival", that Stella is willing to go far as to actually have someone kill Stolas for cheating on her, not caring about who gets in the way.

In "The Circus" it shown that Stella always had a violent temper, even as a child, as a picture of her shows her attacking two quieves. As an adult, she's known to be rather snobby, arrogant and selfish, and during party she made nasty insults about Stolas to her friends, not caring that he was able to hear her. It was also shown Stella can be sadistic as she admits the only reason she comes back to the mansion is to torment Stolas about his affair with Blitzo and would laugh when Stolas dies.

Stella is also shown to be not very intelligent, as in "Western Energy" her brother, Andrealphus, had to frustratingly point out to her that if Striker kills Stolas, she would get nothing, and everything Stolas has would go to Octavia.
ADVERTISEMENT
Gallery

Stella/Gallery
Trivia

The name "Stella" is the Latin word for "star", fitting the astrology theme signature to Stolas.
Stella is the first character in both Hazbin Hotel and Helluva Boss to have a drastic design change from the Helluva Boss pilot.
It is revealed in "The Circus" that Octavia's birth was the sole reason for her and Stolas' marriage, for the sake of an heir to the Goetia Family. It is also revealed that she and Stolas had been arranged to be married since the latter turned of age and had been engaged ever since, up until their marriage.
Based on the twenty-five-year timeskip that follows Stolas' birthday, the two had Octavia when Stolas was only in his late teens or early twenties.
At the end of the episode, she bitterly agrees to discuss a divorce with Stolas.
In one post on Blitzo's non-canon Voxtagram account, he had a horse that had the same name as Stella.
According to Vivziepop, Stella's backstory will be shown, as well as her perspective, and her position in the Goetic society and why it matters so much to her.[4]
Vivziepop explains that while Stella is a villain and a bad person, she also has her own perspective and she was also put into this arranged marriage that she didn't ask for either.[4]
Vivziepop also explains that Stella is very one-note but she does have a perspective that the show the show will get to, however the show isn't about her as it is more about Stolas' perspective.[4]
Vivziepop hearkens Stella's character to the character of BoJack Horseman's mother because they are very similar in that regard.[4]

Striker is a hitman and a major supporting antagonist in Helluva Boss who made his debut in "The Harvest Moon Festival".

Introduced as a farmhand at Rough n' Tumbleweed Ranch, Striker was actually secretly hired by Stella to assassinate Stolas. Later, during his second assassination attempt on Stolas, the hit was called off on Stella's orders as having Stolas alive would have more benefits than having him dead, much to Striker's own chagrin.

In "Oops", Striker had been hired by Crimson as his mafia needed someone for a big score, in which he captured and held Fizzarolli hostage for ransom until his escape alongside Blitzo. In "Mastermind", Striker was summoned as the court witness for the trial against Blitzo.


ADVERTISEMENT
Appearance

Striker is a tall, slim and pale red-skinned imp with a serpentine-like face, and a stature that rivals Blitzo. His eyes have bright yellow sclera, dark green rings around the slit pupils, and black eyelids. He also has a small black mustache, and a mouth full of sharp light yellow teeth inside, with one dull gold fang sticking out.

He has short-cut, ivory-colored hair in a slightly messy style. His horns are ivory-colored and point upwards, however unlike most imps, the stripe pattern is more jagged-styled. He also sports a long tail with four black stripes at the base, and a single black stripe on his tail-fork. He also has eight red and black spikes on the base of his tail.

Striker's attire resembles a southern cowboy, which features a large stereotypical-looking gray hat with his horns protruding, and a red bandana around his neck.

He wears a light gray jacket with slight darker-colored lapels, small yellow cuff links on each of the sleeves' dark gray cuffs, and dark gray trimming in which black tassels can be seen hanging from them. His jacket is usually worn over a black turtleneck which itself is worn under a dark gray vest that is held together by two small yellow buttons. He also wears black fingerless gloves, ivory-colored jeans that are ripped at the thighs, and knee-high, dark gray cowboy boots with red cuffs and toes.

In his debut and in "Mastermind", Striker was seen holding a straw of wheat in his mouth.

After his encounter against Blitzo in "Oops", Striker ended up getting burned on his left eye, leaving a noticeable scar.
ADVERTISEMENT

Personality

Striker is an arrogant, prideful, violent, ruthless, and sadistic individual. He views himself as superior to most of his own kind, having no hesitation to mock and belittle those he views as being beneath him, both physically and mentally, as shown by his constant humiliation and torture of Moxxie.

He holds a deep hatred of the nobility of Hell, deriding them as bluebloods who treat Imps as a lesser class. Because of this, Striker gleefully takes the opportunity to assassinate demons of a higher social standing to prove himself as superior, such as accepting the job to murder Stolas, and mocking him while conversing with Blitzo.

His violent nature belies his sadism. When confronted by Moxxie after his discovery of Striker's blessing-tipped rifle, he chose to corner and attempt to slowly strangle Moxxie to death rather than dispatching him in a faster or less cruel manner. He is also not above random acts of violence against innocents, such as assaulting a by standing Imp for simply getting too close to him.

However, Striker is a cunning, socially smart, manipulative, and fearless person who is willing to show respect towards those he views as acting decisively, even with the odds stacked against them. As demonstrated when he admired that Blitzo was able to start a assassination business in spite of his assertions that Imps rarely succeed in operating businesses in Hell. His manipulative manner is evidenced when he was able to make Blitzo lower his guard by psychologically manipulating him; stating that he was working for lower classes that couldn't care less about him and wasting his great potential by limiting himself to be Stolas' sexual plaything when he could do much better than that, to subsequently suggest that they should work together.

He is able to maintain an aura of fearlessness such as being able to keep a cool head when Blitzo stopped him trying to assassinate Stolas, even cornering the latter against a wall in spite of being held at gunpoint.

He has also been shown to be a highly ambitious individual as he has aspirations above being an assassin and seeks to use his job and connections to gather powerful weapons, with a stated desire to be able to murder powerful hellish entities such as Overlords and demonic nobility. Ironically, he ends up rubbing shoulders with "bluebloods" such as Stella in order to obtain these weapons, though during his interactions with such individuals, he remains polite and conversational. In "Western Energy", Striker shows hatred for demon royalty as he expresses not only eagerness to kill Stolas, but also a personal vendetta against royals, believing all they do is they only talk over lesser demons and take away everything they have.

Unlike the majority of demons, whom are mostly sex-positive, if not outright indecent, even in public, Striker is noticeably much more prudent. Sexual innuendo legitimately irritates him and displays of arousal (especially of the masochistic variety as demonstrated by Moxxie and Stolas) have been shown to shatter his cool-headed facade, if only for a moment. Despite his status as a prude, Striker owns a statue with a large erection in his lair. Also worth noting is that he seems to be able to put his distaste for sexuality aside for the sake of manipulation tactics, demonstrated in the aforementioned scene where he lowered Blitzo's guard.
ADVERTISEMENT

Abilities

Animalistic noises - Striker has a tendency to produce hissing sounds similar to that of a snake or crocodile. His tail can make a rattling sound, moving a certain way similar to that of a rattlesnake.
Ocular illumination - Like many Imps, Striker's eyes emit a light glow in dark areas.
Charisma - Given his skills, strength, charm and good looks, Striker can win the good graces of those around him.
Enhanced endurance - Striker has a great pain tolerance, as he was able to take multiple stabs from Millie from behind and still being able to overpower her while appearing to be unfazed by the wounds. Another example is when Blitzo elbowed his face for almost shooting Moxxie and was able to briefly knock him down later, even being able to quickly escape from the scene despite having received a brutal beating from him, who showed to be strong enough to break a wall with a single punch. In "Oops", he is shown to experience horrible pain by being burned, but still had enough strength to scurry away as he put the fire on himself out.
Enhanced strength - Despite his slim physique, Striker has shown an impressive amount of physical strength. During "The Harvest Moon Festival", Striker was capable of immobilizing and pinning Moxxie, breaking Millie's arm and throwing both of them with ease. He was also able to make Blitzo fall with a single punch during his fight near the end of the episode. In "Western Energy", it also showed he was able to break Stolas' leg by just stomping on it and toss down a large stalactite with his lasso.
Prehensile tail - Striker is shown to be able to use his tail to wield certain weaponry proficiently, such as when he uses Millie's zweihander to attack and defend in the fight against Moxxie and Millie in "Western Energy".
Skillset

Hand-to-hand combat - Striker is shown to be surprisingly proficient in hand-to-hand combat, being able to defend himself from the I.M.P staff. He also uses his tail for unarmed combat as well.
Weapon mastery - He's shown to be skilled with handling various types of weapons especially weapons to kill demons with high status, such as the Carmine-Crafted Blessing-Tipped Rifle. He is also seen being able to use his rope to grab and throw stalactites at Moxxie and Millie.

Musical talent - Striker is shown to have a talent for singing, as shown when he sang his victory tune after he was one of the winners of the Harvest Moon Pain Games.
Guitar-playing - As well as singing, Striker has been shown as being a very good guitar player.

Trivia

Striker seems to possess snake-like traits, such as his tail making a rattling sound when moved a certain way, similar to that of a rattlesnake's, and possessing a snakes snout-like facial features that as an imp appear unique to him and opposing to regular imps.
He has a tendency to produce hissing sounds similar to that of a snake or crocodile, a trait that Blitzo once displayed in "Seeing Stars".
He also has a circular pattern accompanying the pupils of his eyes, similar to the hypnosis eyes of Kaa from The Jungle Book, furthering his snake-like theme. This trait is shown to be shared only with the race of shark-like demons.
In a stream, it was confirmed that Striker is actually an imp hybrid,[1] although, whether or not he is a half imp or only part imp was not disclosed.
Striker's Wanted Poster
Striker's wanted poster
It is shown in "Western Energy" that there are wanted posters of Striker in the Pride and Wrath rings that say "WANTED PREFERABLY DEAD PLEASE", signifying that he is a wanted man throughout at least some of the Rings of Hell.
Striker owns a flip-phone rather than a smartphone like most characters usually have.
According to Fizzarolli in "Oops", Striker has terrible breath.
Development

Striker's appearance went through several drafts and phases in development. His preliminary design was a rough combination of Blitzo and Moxxie's, with later passes shifting to a reptilian/snake-like direction.[3][4]
Inspiration for Striker's design came from Rattlesnake Jake from Rango, Snidely Whiplash from The Rocky and Bullwinkle Show, Angel Eyes from The Good, the Bad and the Ugly, and the 1970 Mexican film, El Topo.[5]

Succubi are a subspecies of Hellborn Demons that have the second lowest ranking in Hell's hierarchy along with other unknown demon species.[1]

The species are known to have sexually intensifying abilities to humans.

Description

Succubi demons are in the second-lowest ranking tier in terms of Hell's hierarchy, ranking just above Imps and Hellhounds.

They are one of the few demons that are allowed access to the human world in order to do their jobs of seducing humans, the exact reasons for these actions are unknown. While in the living realm, they shapeshift into human forms as disguises to avoid detection from humans.
Notable Succubi

Appearance

Stu, a male succubus hybrid
Succubi possess voluptuous, yet human-like figures, stocky to slender, and have color schemes consist of black and red with a pinkish hue. They have black-tipped horns, a barbed tail, and small bat-like wings sprouting from their backs. The tip of their tail can be triangular or heart-like shaped. Succubi have yellow sclera with pink or red irises. They also possess human-like feet.

Succubi have some biological similarities to imps, including the lack of an obvious nose. Albeit, succubi are taller, have smaller horns, and possess more varied skin tones of pink and red. Some succubi also possess (pointed) ears, a rare trait for a demon.

Hair colors vary between succubi. They can be brunette, ravenette, grey, blonde, or even pink. Succubi can also be bald.

Abilities

Erokinesis - All succubi have the ability to enhance sexual desire in humans by exuding a supernatural allure, allowing them to seduce their targets. It is unknown to what degree regular demons are effected by this. However, Hellhounds appear to be either immune or resistant to these effects. The exact strength a succubi's manipulation against a human is unknown, as a small contingent of human law enforcement officers appeared initially unaffected by the presence of a group of succubi, whereas a large gathering of (alcohol inhibited) human partygoers were overwhelmingly affected by their presence.
Sexual Inducement - Succubi have the ability to trigger the sex hormones of anyone they make contact with upon sight, touch, or voice, and triggers anyone to become sexually active.
Human Shapeshifting - Certain succubi have the ability to project and shapeshift into any human form that they see fit. Some succubi cannot perfectly shapeshift, leaving some notable defects such as pointed ears or unnatural colored eyes.
Flight - All succubi have wings which allows them to fly.
Mortality

In "The Full Moon", a male succubus demon was shot in the head by a regular bullet from Collin's exoskeleton rifle and died, revealing that succubi can die to non-angelic weaponry, like imps and hellhounds.

Trivia

In mythology, the succubus is a demon that targets humans for sexual pleasure, though often causing suffering to their human partners in exchange for this. They are traditionally depicted as the embodiment of lust itself, as such they possess seductive figures, and are imbued with supernatural allure in order to captivate potential victims.
Traditionally, the term "succubus" refers to a female lust demon that targets men for sex, designating all succubi as female. Whereas, male succubi are referred to as "incubus", and traditionally target women for sex.
In the series, while incubi exist,[1] none have been identified; furthermore, all the members of Verosika's group have been collectively called succubi,[5][6] even though some of them are male.
Incubi were first officially mentioned in The King of Lust: Asmodeus, a grimoire seen in the episode, "The Circus".
The Talmudic figure Lilith is often associated with the succubus demon, if not the mother of all succubi and incubi, in occultism and Western folklore. Although Lilith is confirmed to be the same character in the series, it is unknown if she is connected to the species.
The aforementioned grimoire has a segment on "Asmodean Crystals". The segment, written in Nordic runes, translates as: "Bestowed to mainly Succubi and Incubi by the Sin of Lust, these crystals allow access to the mortal realm." This implies that, much like Stolas' personal grimoire, these crystals serve as a Succubus' only means to access the living world and must be obtained and registered by Asmodeus himself. This is reinforced in "The Full Moon", when, after Stolas gifts Blitzo with his own Asmodean Crystal, reveals that he would be under Asmodeus' name to use it.
The building I.M.P Headquarters is located in apparently has an entire floor dedicated to one or more succubus companies according to Vortex.
Due to their nature linked to sexual activities, Succubi are commonly found transiting in the Lust Ring, both as employees of establishments present there, and as customers of the different services provided there.
It is shown that when a succubus attempts to attract humans, they release images of floating hearts. It is unknown if these hearts are actually visible in-universe or if they are just meant for the viewers to know which of them are succubi.

Tilla is the deceased mother of Blitzo and Barbie Wire, and wife of Cash Buckzo, who was first pictured in the non-canon Helluva Boss pilot and later pictured in the main series episode "Ozzie's" .

Appearance

Tilla appeared to be a tall, slim and red-skinned imp with long, shaggy charcoal hair, eyes with red irises and yellow sclera, and a pair of thin white-striped black horns. Like the rest of the all-imp circus, she had a heart-skull marking on her forehead.

In pictures, she is depicted wearing a long-sleeved purple robe-like dress. She also wore a charm that is identical to the one Blitzo wears in present time.
Pilot

In the pilot, Tilla had a similar appearance but had completely black horns, shorter and lighter-colored hair, lighter-colored skin from below the eyes and nose, and white marks on both eyelids and on her chest up to the left of her neck. She instead wore what appeared to be a maroon sleeveless dress with brown-and-white sashes, and brown opera gloves.

Personality

While Tilla appears very little in the series, given the fact that Blitzo remembers her with fondness and mourns her death, it can be said that, in contrast to the manipulative and abusive Cash, she was a gentle, kind and loving mother to both him and Barbie Wire.
Relationships

Family

Cash Buckzo

Cash is Tilla's husband. Her relationship with him is obscure. In "The Circus", Cash convinces Blitzo to burglarize the Goetia family on the grounds that it would benefit their family, mentioning helping him and Tilla. However, while this may suggest that he holds some degree of care for his wife, it's clear that Cash is merely bringing her up as a means to manipulate their son Blitzo. This could indicate that he has no qualms using his children's love for her if monetary gain is promised. While she is shown to care for the children they had together, her feelings for Cash are currently unknown.

Blitzo

Blitzo is Tilla's son. While not having been shown interacting it can be assumed that Blitzo was very close to his mother, as Cash was able to convince him to do what he was told to help his mother. At the end of "Ozzie's", Blitzo ultimately breaks down when he comes across a family photo where he and Barbie Wire gave their mother a birthday card. In "Oops", it is revealed that his mother died in the circus fire, causing Blitzo great trauma over her death, and blaming himself for it as shown in "Ghostf**kers". Blitzo also has been keeping Tilla's skull charm ever since she perished.

Barbie Wire

Barbie Wire is Tilla's daughter. While the two have yet to interact on-screen, it can be inferred that Barbie had a loving relationship with her mother, as in family photos, Tilla often has her arms lovingly around her daughter.

History

Past

At some point during her life, she met Cash Buckzo, with whom she had twins, Blitzo and Barbie Wire.

Fifteen years before the events of "Oops", Tilla perished in a fire that Blitzo accidentally started at Cash Buckzo's circus.[2][1]

Helluva Boss Season 1

"Ozzie's"

After Blitzo returns home from a bad night, depressed, he lays on his couch and looks through photos on his phone, breaking down into tears when seeing a picture of his mother and sister.

Helluva Boss Season 2

"Ghostf**kers"

Tilla appears as one of Blitzo's visions when he is being tormented by Rolando.

Trivia

The name Tilla is of German origin, which means "Battle strength". It is derived from the name "Mathilda".
The red skull charm she is shown wearing in pictures is identical to the one that Blitzo wears in present time, hinting that Blitzo's charm came from her.
The same skull charm is drawn on a part of Blitzo's Boss Goals board in his office in the Helluva Boss pilot.
Development

Her first appearance was in the non-canon Helluva Boss pilot in a poster in Blitzo's office with a third imp named Barbie Wire, advertising them as "The Amazing Imp Siblings", thus implying that the three were siblings. However, in the official series, the poster was changed to exclude Tilla, and the text was changed to be "The Amazing Imp Twins".
In the episode "Ozzie's", a female imp with a strong resemblance to Tilla is shown in Blitzo's phone gallery with him and Barbie Wire, who are both holding a card with "happy berth moma" written on it, implying this imp is their mother, which was later confirmed by one of the show's animators.[3] After the release of "Ghostf**kers", an official piece of merchandise used the name "Tilla" for their mother, confirming that the character of Tilla had been moved to be Blitzo and Barbie Wire's mother.[4]

Vassago is a Prince of the Ars Goetia[2] and a supporting character of Helluva Boss who made his debut in the episode "Mastermind", after originally appearing in the Hazbin Hotel pilot.

Appearance

Vassago is a lanky avian demon who greatly resembles a Scarlet macaw, with red feathers, a white face, and a hooked black beak. He also has rather long, gold-tipped purple feathers on the back of his head with a gold-colored streak through the center, and red eyes with no irises or pupils, which are often covered by a pair of yellow visor-shades that vaguely resemble a star or crown.

Vassago wears a red suit-jacket with a gold-trimmed popped-collar, black lapels, a star brooch, a giant "X" and a small star design on the back, and rather long, extravagant tails that are trimmed with black, the top part being purple while the bottom is a gradient of two shades of orange. Over this, he wears a white dress-shirt with two black buttons on the center.

Vassago's clothing also features black pants and white arm-length gloves and thigh-high high-heeled boots - his gloves having black torn-like cuffs and two red stripes in the front, while his boots have black toes and tips of the heels, as well as an "X" shape on the bottom center.
Personality

Vassago is shown to be a high-strung and mindful demon within Hell's royal hierarchy, though unlike most of the aristocratic elite, he holds the responsibilities of Hell's governance in high regard. As such, he expressed a distaste for unfairness and harm, especially when the matter of another Goetia such as Stolas was involved. This was shown during Blitzo's trial when he noted Stolas' absence and advocated that he needed to be brought in, then being genuinely disturbed when Andrealphus accused Blitzo of being responsible for the assassination attempt on Stolas. Similarly, he expressed annoyance toward Andrealphus' condescending attitude and his attempts to win the case against Stolas going so far as to call Andrealphus an arrogant idiot for his comments.

Vassago has a tendency to slip between English and Spanish in conversations, although he seems to slip into the latter more at times of high emotion. He also seems to have a whimsical taste for music, as he cheered for Stolas presenting his defense in song.
Abilities

Vassago walking on his star platform
Vassago's star-shaped platform
Immortality - As demonic royalty, Vassago is biologically immortal, being able to live for a long period of time and only able to be killed by angelic weaponry.

Skillset

Bilingualism - Vassago speaks both English and Spanish very fluently.
History

Hazbin Hotel pilot

When Vaggie explained to Angel Dust about Alastor's origins, Vassago can be seen alongside several Overlords.

Helluva Boss Season 2

"Mastermind"

During Blitzo's trial, Vassago demanded that the trial needed Stolas' presence to proceed. He then became annoyed by Andrealphus, who proceeded to have an argument with him. When Stolas finally arrived at the court, Vassago cheered for his arrival and for singing, but was shocked to listen to Stolas claiming to have committed the crime. Regardless, he was summarily sympathetic and saddened to witness Stolas losing his powers and status.

Relationships

"YES! Yes! Cántalo, baby! [Sing it, baby!]"
―Vassago, to Stolas
Vassago holds Stolas in a positive regard. He was upset that Stolas was not present during a trial that was about him, and was glad that Stolas had arrived to maintain the trial's fairness, and eager to hear the latter sing. Although shocked by Stolas' confession, Vassago still felt saddened after witnessing Stolas being revoked of his powers and status.

Andrealphus

"¡NO me voy a callar, (I will NOT shut up,) pendejo arrogante! (you arrogant idiot!)"
―Vassago, to Andrealphus
Vassago and Andrealphus dislike each other vehemently, with them getting into a heated argument during the trial in "Mastermind" after Vassago was provoked by Andrealphus' condescending personality.

Employees of I.M.P

Blitzo

Like the other members inside the courtroom, Vassago didn't understand Blitzo's sarcasm and genuinely believed Blitzo would hurt Stolas. However, he believed that the trial itself was unfair, while also being surprised by Stolas' confession of having used the imp.

Vassago is based on the demon of the same name from The Lesser Key of Solomon, who is a prince "of good nature".
In a tweet, Vivziepop stated that Vassago is "a very good boy".[4]
Vivziepop confirmed in an Instagram moments that Vassago will appear in Season 3.[5]
Prior to his appearance in Helluva Boss, Vassago first appeared in the pilot episode of Hazbin Hotel, where he was seen among the Overlords in Vaggie's story about Alastor, implying he was part of the ranking. It is unknown if his status as an Overlord will be carried over into the main series and its spin-off.

"How do you think I felt? When the fun guy I was dating decided to just bail on me because I made the shitty mistake of saying I love... Ugh! It was the most embarrassing feeling. ―Verosika Mayday, explaining to Blitzo how upset she was at him
Verosika Mayday is a succubus demon and a famous popstar in both Hell and the living world.

She is Blitzo's ex-girlfriend and a recurring character in Helluva Boss who made her debut alongside her crew in "Spring Broken".


ADVERTISEMENT
Appearance

Verosika is a tall, hot pink-skinned succubus demoness with an hourglass figure. She sports a long, black-tipped spade-shaped tail and a pair of black-tipped horns on top of her head with black star designs on them; the left one taller than the right. She also has a pair of bat-like wings on her back, with black markings that resemble heart shapes.

Her eyes have white-outlined light pink irises, yellow sclera, slit pupils, long and thick eyelashes protruding from them, and a small heart-shaped beauty mark under the right eye. She also has long knee-length hair colored in ombre-white, with pink undertones from lighter to darker towards the tips, and a darker-colored stripe across her bangs.

On her right arm is a red heart tattoo with Blitzo's name on it that has been crossed out by a thick black "X". Her mouth sports black lips and small fangs inside.

Verosika wears a black choker necklace and a tightly-fitted, black and white minidress with a contrasting "X" and "O" shapes on the chest, as well as a star design at the abdomen. She also wore long black leg sleeves with three hot pink "X" designs down the sides, and black high-heels which sport a vague heart motif.

She accessorizes with a set of white arm-length gloves with the right having the same "X" patterns as her leg sleeves (albeit thinner), a pale pink fur coat which vaguely matches her hair, and a pair of round gold-framed shades which have pink heart designs on each of their maroon lenses.
Human Disguise

In her human disguise, Verosika takes the appearance of a light brown-skinned woman with her eyes now having white sclera. Her long hair is ombre blonde with pink undertones from darker to lighter towards the tips, along with auburn roots and a light pink streak down the length.

She appears noticeably taller in her human disguise than her regular appearance, and her arm tattoo does not appear in her human disguise.

Her outfit changes to a white-trimmed, two-piece pink ruffled mini dress - her crop-top sporting long sleeves with her right sleeve being detached, while her miniskirt's ruffles are colored in a slight darker shade. The skirt also includes a white star design on the front and a black heart on the hip, along with dovetails which forms into a light pink sash with slight darker-colored ruffles, and a heart design that visually references to her tail.

She also wears the same choker, thigh-highs and heels as before, minus the 'X' cutouts.

ADVERTISEMENT

Personality

As a succubus demon, Verosika is actively seductive and flirtatious, attributes she integrates into her famous popstar persona as a means of manipulation. Despite her status as a star, her fame, and her confidence, she also appears somewhat jaded and is nursing a drinking problem, something she has previously been to rehab for.

Verosika is highly competitive, but she also is petty and mean-spirited. She doesn't take losing well, particularly to Blitzo, with whom she shares a romantic history - a relationship that did not end well, leading to her bitterness and pettiness towards him. In "Apology Tour", when she and Blitzo spoke, she reveals that she truly loved Blitzo and was embarrassed for being vulnerable and saying she loved him and him bailing on her, which resulted in her bitterness and anger towards him. But, on one end, she truly wants to see Blitzo change into a better person, and, while she may not forgive him entirely, she slowly began to lose the bitterness she felt towards him, even offering him a slice of cake while also teasingly calling him a "fuckwad". In "Mastermind", Verosika showed great concern and horror when she saw him about to be executed.

Despite being Succubi, Verosika and her group appear to have certain standards when in comes to sexual partners. This is shown when they cringed and groaned in disgust at the thought of pleasuring the cops after they were arrested at the end of "Spring Broken".

In "Apology Tour", she showed that she empathizes with others. She is willing to help people who have been hurt by Blitzo like herself cope, albeit unhealthily, by throwing a party dedicated to hating Blitzo. She even encourages Stolas to speak out on his feelings after being hurt by Blitzo and she calls him the "freshest ex".
ADVERTISEMENT
Abilities

Demon Transformation - Verosika can transform into a larger "full demon" form at will, the silhouette of which can be seen when she and her gang cornered Moxxie in their newly rented office.
Human Disguise - Verosika can take on a convincing human appearance to disguise herself in the living world.
Sexual Inducement - Verosika has the ability to trigger a human's sex drive with her singing voice, touch, and even just her presence. Humans in her vicinity become extremely amorous and seek to make sexual contact with those around them, including Verosika's gang of succubi. This power appears to only actively affect humans, as demons such as Hellhounds near her retain control of themselves and their senses, whether they are using a human disguise or not.
Skillset

Musical Talent - Verosika is a gifted singer. This skill can amplify her seductive power and induce humans who hear her to fall under her amorous charms.
Enhanced Strength - She was strong enough to kick a bar off of a house stair railing.
ADVERTISEMENT

Gallery

Verosika Mayday/Gallery
Trivia

Verosika's first name is a reference to the feminine name "Veronica" while her last name, Mayday, is a reference to the radio distress signals usually sent by ships and aircrafts.
Additionally, her name also shares the same initials as the show creator, Vivienne Medrano.
Verosika was not immediately confirmed to be a succubus, although there were many indications that she was intended as such. Not only because of her appearance, but also her alluring effect on humans, which is an ability succubi are traditionally depicted as using to ensnare prey.
Blitzo's derogatory nickname for her, "succu-bitch", added to the idea, as well as her car's license plate, which reads "SUCK-4-LIFE".
Her pop song, "Vacay to Bonetown", features lyrics which also directly mention succubi.
She was eventually confirmed to be a succubus in art sent to Cristina Vee from the show's animators.
Similar to Robo Fizz and formerly Fizzarolli, Verosika also pronounces the now-silent "o" in Blitzo's name. This is possibly for the dual reasons of her potentially knowing him while he was still using the full pronunciation, and also knowing that it now irritates him to hear, as he has intentionally distanced himself from it. However, after she and Blitzo spoke and he apologized, their relationship slowly began to heal, where Verosika calls his name with the silent "o".
Verosika has implied that she knows Blitzo's sister, Barbie Wire. She indirectly mentions her when verbally sparring with Blitzo, telling him, "So, your sister says 'Hi'". Although, whether she is telling the truth or just attempting to bait Blitzo is currently unknown.
The heart on her cheek could be a reference to Marina Diamandis during her "Electra Heart" era, during which she also famously had a black heart on her cheek (albeit, the left one as opposed to Verosika wearing it on her right). According to the lyrics of Diamandis' song "How to Be a Heartbreaker", wearing a heart on the cheek is one of the rules of being a heartbreaker, which also fits Verosika's situation with Blitzo.
Her Sinstagram username is simply "verosika", as revealed in the episode "Seeing Stars".
A Chibi-style keychain of Verosika's human form appears as part of the art seller's wares in "Seeing Stars".
Vivienne Medrano did a lot of work on Verosika's design, with help from Cécilia Goncalves[6] who made her human disguise.[7]
Sam Haft said in a tweet that he desperately wants to make more Verosika songs.[8]
In an interview posted on December 10, 2023, Sam Haft stated that there is definitely more Verosika to come.[9]

Verosika's crew[1][2] are a group of Succubi Demons who are friends with Verosika Mayday.

They are supporting characters who made their debut alongside Verosika in the episode "Spring Broken".

Appearance

Default

The multitude of Verosika's crew take the appearance of stereotypical succubi demons, including pink skin, curved horns, fangs, and forked tails.

Human Disguise

Their human disguises look almost identical to their default demon forms, minus the horns, wings, and tails. Instead of red/pink skin, they take on human skin colors from every race, but most retain their red pupils.

Personality

Like Verosika, her crew is known to be very seductive and sexually active, as shown when they found Moxxie adorable and attempted having sex with him.

However, unlike Verosika, her friends appear to be much less cunning and cold-hearted. They are also shown to be much more fearful than her, as they all cowered in fear of being arrested.

Despite being Succubi, they appear to have certain standards when it comes to sexual partners and prefer to choose them, cringing in disgust at the thought of needing to pleasure the cops after they are arrested at the end of "Spring Broken".

In "Apology Tour", several of them attend Verosika's "Anti-Blitzo" party. It is unknown if they ever had any sort of past relation to Blitzo before becoming a part of Verosika's crew, or if they only came to support Verosika similarly to Vortex.

However, this effect only works on humans since demons appear to be immune to the effects, as seen when Josh tried to do this to Loona it had no effect.

Vortex is the bodyguard of the famous pop star Verosika Mayday, and the boyfriend of the Sin of Gluttony, Beelzebub.

He is a supporting character who made his debut alongside Verosika and her crew in "Spring Broken".


ADVERTISEMENT
Appearance

Vortex is a tall and muscular hellhound who, similar to Loona, sports a wolf-like appearance and a gray color scheme, only darker. He has a dog-like muzzle with a large black nose and sharp teeth inside, a bushy tail with dark gray tips, and black claws protruding from his fingers and toes.

His fur is a few tones of gray, with his head and ears being colored in a rather dark shade of gray, along with a black, tattoo-like fur-pattern shaped like a wolf's head on his left arm. He also has thick black eyebrows and eyes with dark gray upper-eyelids - his right eye sports a red sclera with a white iris, while his left is blind and has a red scar across it, which also makes his left brow slit. Both his ears are slightly ripped.

Vortex wears a ripped black tank top under a dark gray leather jacket with rips on the hem and the sleeves being ripped off, along with lighter-colored lapels and red spikes on the front of the sleeves. He also wears a pair of ripped, dark gray knee-length shorts.
Human Disguise

Vortex's human disguise is greatly similar to his hellhound form, albeit he takes the appearance of a tall, dark brown-skinned man with a slightly ragged ear, thick dark brown eyebrows and hair styled into a buzz-cut. In addition, his right eye changes into a white sclera with a red iris.

His clothing is exactly the same, but with the addition of black pointed shoes.

ADVERTISEMENT

Personality

As a bodyguard, Vortex is intimidating at first glance, but is otherwise very approachable and friendly with other hellhounds such as Loona. He's essentially a laid-back guy who knows when to get serious, with a simultaneously laid back and no-nonsense attitude, especially when it comes to his job.

He'll happily strike up a conversation with someone he can see means no harm but will not hesitate to knock someone out if they get too close to his boss.

As the bodyguard and a friend of Verosika, he supports and protects her. In "Apology Tour", he sings along with Verosika about Blitzo being a "motherfucker" as backup for Stolas, even though he never had any personal grudge or hatred against Blitzo.
Abilities

Human disguise - Vortex can take on a convincing human appearance to disguise himself in the living world.
Enhanced strength - He has displayed an incredible amount of strength which lands him his job as Verosika's bodyguard.
Skillset

Driving - He is seen driving Verosika's car in his debut episode, with the latter in the front passenger's seat.
Musical talent - In "Apology Tour", he sings along with Verosika and Stolas.
ADVERTISEMENT
Gallery

Vortex/Gallery
Trivia

The name "Vortex" refers to a "mass of whirling fluid and or air" akin to that of a whirlpool or whirlwind.
Vortex is the first male hellhound shown in Helluva Boss, and the first male hellhound shown in the Hazbin Hotel franchise as a whole.
Cécilia Goncalves made the design of Vortex's Human Disguise.[2]
He shares the same voice actor as Asmodeus in Helluva Boss, as well as the lizard sinner seen with Zeezi in Klub Kaiju in the Hazbin Hotel pilot and Zestial in the Hazbin Hotel main series, with all of them being voiced by James Monroe Iglehart.
It is revealed through Loona's phone in "Seeing Stars" that his Sinstagram username is simply his own name.
Meanwhile, in "Queen Bee", it is shown that Vortex's name in her contacts is "Tex!

Wally Wackford is a recurring character in Helluva Boss who made his debut in "Loo Loo Land".

His main role in the show is a running gag wherein he appears to be working a different job in every episode he appears in.

Appearance

Wally is a carny-like imp with muted crimson skin, curled black and white horns, a triangle-tipped tail, white hair, and black eyes with yellow sclera. He also has a long curly mustache. As seen in the April Fools 2025 merchandise, Wally's body is covered in a variety of numerous white scars.[3][4]

He typically wears a white regency shirt, sleeve garters, gray vest, black Kentucky colonel tie, white pants with gray stripes, and black boots. Starting from "C.H.E.R.U.B", Wally wears a top hat with a pale lavender gray stripe.

In "Ozzie's", Wally is dressed like a bartender, wearing a large purple top hat with a cyan section that has a heart on it. He wears a purple vest, which is orange on the inside, and underneath he wears a white shirt with two orange buttons.[5]
Young

As a child, Wally wore big round glasses, purple overalls and shirt with a black ribbon bow.[6]

Personality

Wally Wackford is a businessman who attempts to sell products for money. He runs a company called Wacky Wally Wackford's Wacky Idea "Factory" where people invent stuff, and he attempts to make money off of their inventions. He was also formerly a torch seller at Loo Loo Land before the park's destruction.

He has been shown to be a somewhat goofy and eccentric individual in his actions, an example being when he would be the only one laughing after making a lame pun or joke.
Gallery

Wally Wackford/Gallery
Trivia

Before being spoken in "C.H.E.R.U.B", Wally's name was first confirmed in a tweet by Don Darryl Rivera.[7]
He speaks with a stereotypical Southern accent, similar to Foghorn Leghorn from Looney Tunes, even right down to starting his commercial with saying, "I say, I say", which the latter was known for.
His design was inspired by the old-time hucksters and snake oil salesmen.[8]
Like Fizzarolli, Robo Fizz, and Verosika Mayday, he pronounces the "O" in Blitzo's name.
He shares the same voice actor as Cletus, Travis, and Mister Butler, with the four of them being voiced by Don Darryl Rivera.
There was originally going to be a laugh track for him at the end of the episode, "C.H.E.R.U.B", but, then there was a problem with the audio. So, they decided to make him laugh at himself instead.[9]
Despite not having a real-life Instagram counterpart, his Sinstagram username is revealed to be "wacky_wally.official" in the episode "Seeing Stars".
As revealed in the episode "MAMMON'S MAGNIFICENT MUSICAL MID-SEASON SPECIAL (ft Fizzarolli)", Wally Wackford is actually younger than Fizzarolli and Blitzo.[6]
According to Vivziepop, because of a fan theory about Wally Wackford secretly being Mammon, she made a point to put the two characters in a scene together to disprove the theory.[10]
Despite appearing in an official artwork posted by the Helluva Boss Twitter in celebration of Pride Month 2024, Wally is the only character shown who is not in any pride or sexuality flag colors.[11] However, in a reply Wally is confirmed to canonically be a "Silly Little Guy".[12]

―I.M.P jingle
The Immediate Murder Professionals, abbreviated as I.M.P, is a startup assassination business within Hell. The founder and CEO is Blitzo, and their office is located in the seventh floor of a condemned company building.

The company originally operated illegally with the use of Stolas' Grimoire, but as of "The Full Moon", having received an Asmodean Crystal, are conducting business legally under Asmodeus' jurisdiction.

Description

I.M.P was founded by Blitzo and is run by him along with his employees, consisting of fellow Imps, Moxxie and Millie, as well as his adoptive Hellhound daughter, Loona. The company offers the unique service of eliminating living targets still on Earth as a form of settling the unfinished business of Hell's residents.

This was previously done through the use of Stolas' Grimoire that opened portals to Earth, allowing the assassins access to their human targets. However, as of "The Full Moon", they now use an Asmodean Crystal that was given to Blitzo by Stolas.

While they do not accept contracts unless the targets are in the living world, they may accept special requests either if enough money is offered or they get to kill someone; an example of this is shown when Stolas hired them as bodyguards in order to safely visit Loo Loo Land with his daughter and they got to kill several would-be assassins targeting Stolas.
History

At some point before the start of the series, Blitzo started a freelance assassination business, I.M.P, which began as an operation in Hell.[1][2]

At some point, while Blitzo was imprisoned in the Greed Ring, he met his cellmate Moxxie.[1] At some point after their escape, Blitzo hired Moxxie.[3]

At some point after Blitzo opened I.M.P, he hired Loona as their receptionist.

Sometime before the start of the series, after poaching a hit from Blitzo and Moxxie, seeing her potential, Blitzo tracked Millie down in order to recruit her. After a bar fight, Blitzo hired Millie.[2]

Prior to the series, Blitzo attempted to break into Stolas' mansion to steal the Goetic Prince's grimoire in order to obtain access to the living world. After being caught and then alone with the prince, Blitzo seduced Stolas and escaped with the grimoire the next morning.[4]

Blitzo then leased a rundown office space to be their headquarters, and using the grimoire he had stolen from Stolas, Blitzo went on to formally establish I.M.P as a business of killing humans on Earth for sinners.[2]

In the non-canon Helluva Boss pilot, it was shown in the commercial that a sinner from Ohio had hired I.M.P, in a flashback that Stolas had hired I.M.P to kill a political candidate convincing people global warming exists, and an unknown client who hired I.M.P to kill Eddie.

In "Murder Family", I.M.P are hired by a sinner named Mrs. Mayberry to kill the woman who ruined her life, but before the job, Moxxie accidentally sets fire to their office, with Loona securing the grimoire. During the job, Stolas calls Blitzo and offers an exchange wherein they meet on the full moon each month so Stolas can use his grimoire followed by a night of sexual relations, but for the rest of the time I.M.P can keep and use the grimoire to continue illegally doing their business, and with no other choice Blitzo agreed.

In "Loo Loo Land", Stolas hires I.M.P as bodyguards for his and Octavia's trip to Loo Loo Land.

In "Spring Broken", after Verosika Mayday steals the I.M.P parking spot, Blitzo issues a challenge to assassinate more humans than her crew can have sex with. Blitzo creates a flyer for discount service and I.M.P is hired to kill numerous spring breakers, however, after Millie kills the monster Verosika accidentally created they agree to keep it secret as long as I.M.P can use their parking space.

In "C.H.E.R.U.B", I.M.P are hired by a sinner named Loopty Goopty to kill his best friend and business partner, Lyle Lipton. During the job, I.M.P come up against members of C.H.E.R.U.B, who try to save and change the heart of their target.

In "Truth Seekers", after a successful hit and on their way back to hell, things go awry when D.H.O.R.K.S. agents One and Two capture Blitzo and Moxxie, requiring Millie and Loona to rescue them.

In "Ozzie's", I.M.P return to the headquarters after doing a job killing lumberjacks.

In "Seeing Stars", Octavia steals the grimoire that allows I.M.P to do their job, however, when Loona tracks her down in Los Angeles and brings her back, the book is returned to I.M.P.

In "Exes and Oohs", I.M.P are brought to the Greed Ring under the pretense of it being a business venture in hell, but arrive to find it was a setup by Moxxie's father to get Moxxie there and marry Chaz into their mafia.

In "Unhappy Campers", a sinner comes to hire I.M.P to investigate his murder, but as Blitzo is too busy, Moxxie is placed in charge to accomplish the hit. However, the job takes five days to complete.

In "The Full Moon", on the day of the full moon, I.M.P return to the headquarters after doing a job and Blitzo begins preparing for his rendezvous with Stolas in order to keep using Stolas' grimoire. That night, Stolas ends their arrangement and takes back his grimoire, however, he gifts Blitzo an Asmodean Crystal so that I.M.P can continue doing their job but legally under Asmodeus' jurisdiction.

In "Ghostf**kers", I.M.P are facing bankruptcy due to Blitzo spending all their funds to cope with his breakup with Stolas, and has not been paying the employees for a month. Blitzo and Millie take a job by a sinner named Rita to find and kill a supposed ghost haunting a spooky hotel.

In "Mastermind", I.M.P is still recovering from bankruptcy but is met by enthusiastic demons who are willing to work as interns for the company. I.M.P is almost endangered when the crew are arrested for their illegal activities and put on trial for execution, but subsequently gains popularity when they become the first Hellborns to survive a trial. Some demons even emailed Blitzo, some of them asking if the organization is hiring.

In "Sinsmas", I.M.P is celebrating the holiday of the same name in their headquarters. Stolas takes on the role of being their receptionist, which allows Loona to join the three on a mission. A sinner comes into the office to hire I.M.P to murder her ex-husband who cheated on her with another man, a situation similar to Blitzo and Stolas'. After seeing the happy family, Blitzo calls the hit off and throws the client out of the building.
Advertising

Blitzo has made several expensive advertising campaigns with varying degrees of effectiveness.
I.M.P Jingle

Main article: I.M.P Jingle
In the non-canon Helluva Boss pilot, a series of TV adverts prominently starring Blitzo and featuring a jingle that he wrote. Much to Moxxie's annoyance, Blitzo used up most of his employees' salaries funding it, paying for it to be run for three hours straight on an unpopular TV channel, then blamed Moxxie for the company's poor performance.

Billboard

A single billboard near I.M.P Headquarters, Blitzo attempted to have it say "Got an asshole in the living world? Come to I.M.P!" with a big picture of Blitzo and a giant arrow pointing to the I.M.P office. The advertising company instead used poor-quality speech-to-text software when making it, with the billboard reading "Goat an asshole in the living worlds!? Come to I Am Pee!!!!??! Make sure you put this sign on the rite side. Don't fuck this up. Also payment may take a few weeks because it cums in the mail. SPEECH TO TEXT. Blitzo.", and pointed the arrow away from the office.

Spring Break flyer

In "Spring Broken", Blitzo made this promotional flyer during his challenge with Verosika Mayday over a parking spot, advertising a discount for contracts for that day. Despite Blitzo only creating one flyer (and Moxxie saying that the flyer contained poor spelling and bad grammar), it was proved to be wildly successful and attracted a line of customers stretching down the street.

Imp City is one of the cities of Hell, and the primary setting of Helluva Boss. It is home to the imp demons, the lowest in society, along with Hell's homeless.

It is shown to be located in the Second Circle of the Pride Ring.

Description

Due to Imp City being in the Pride Ring it has a red sky. The city is shown to have grey or dark red buildings with some yellow windows, as well as sometimes pink windows.

The city has a black rimmed sign with an eye symbol and the words "Welcome to: IMP CITY", with "SECOND CIRCLE" underneath. The sign has a red half pentagram at the bottom and a pair of imp-like horns at the top.

Within Imp City is I.M.P Headquarters, which is a black and dark gray building with black and white horns built onto it, and has some black windows and antennas attached on it.

There is also a spiked dark grey, gold, and red building with what seems to be an observatory on top that has a red lens with a black pupil peeking out of it, as well as having one larger dark red spike at the back of it.

There is also a blank billboard on one of the buildings.

Imp City appears extremely shabby and rundown, even by Hell's standards.
Notable Locations

I.M.P Headquarters
Moxxie and Millie's apartment
Blitzo's apartment
Trivia

Though it is called "Imp City", there are other types of demons in the city, such as Succubi and Hellhounds.
While it is located in the Pride Ring, the billboard indicates that it is located in the "Second Circle". Given its differing name, it could allude to the Nine Circles of Hell that Katie Killjoy mentioned in the Hazbin Hotel pilot.
The Nine Circles of Hell are the locations visited during Dante's journey in Inferno of Dante Alighieri's Divine Comedy.
In "Spring Broken" and the non-canon Helluva Boss Pilot, the welcome sign indicates that Imp City was established in 1981, possibly implying that the city's founding date is a reference to The Imp, a horror film released that year.

The Pride Ring is one of the seven Rings of Hell and is the first and topmost ring within Hell.

Sinners are confined to and can only exist in this ring, however, like the other rings in Hell, the Pride Ring is accessible and traversable by Hellborn species.[1][2]

Description

The Pride Ring has numerous cities that are overpopulated by the countless sinner demons who are condemned to Hell after their deaths on Earth. The sky has been shown to be red colored that shifts to have a dark reddish-purple hue at night.[3] Also from this ring, the pentagram moon and Heaven are visible in the sky. Its full moon is a glowing orb with light swirling around it.

This ring experiences yearly attacks by the Exorcists in order to quell the overpopulation crisis and prevent an uprising from Hell's Sinner population. As per Lucifer's pardon from Heaven, the Hellborn of the Pride Ring, and by extension the rest of Hell, are to be spared from the Extermination.

The realm may be inspired by the nine circles of Hell from Dante Alighieri's Inferno. While presented as the top ring in Hazbin Hotel, there is no circle of pride mentioned in Inferno, instead the first circle is said to be limbo. Pride is actually the first terrace of Mount Purgatory in the Purgatorio, part of Dante's Divine Comedy.
The Pride Ring was the first of the seven rings to be introduced.
This is the only ring to be seen in both Hazbin Hotel and Helluva Boss.
According to the "Mammon's Clown Pageant" shirt merchandise, the Pride Ring has a location called "The Royal Circle".[4][5] However, it is currently not known whether the information listed on the shirt is canon in the show.
