St. Peter is a pale-skinned slim angel with curled, short pale-blonde hair, turquoise eyes with no pupils, and sharp-styled eyebrows colored royal blue. As an angel, he sports a white halo above his head, and a pair of large feathered wings on his back which are celeste blue and cream-colored.

He wears a light blue vest over a pale yellow shirt with the long sleeves sporting dull golden cuffs, and a light blue skirt with dull golden detailing that forms into a cross at the hem over a high-collared. He also wears a pastel red bowtie, and for footwear, he wears dull golden flats.
Personality

St. Peter appears to be a friendly person overall. He is welcoming to newcomers and visitors, even if they're demons. He is somewhat flirty, enjoying the company of attractive people, especially a muscular female angel.

However he is somewhat prone to being startled, freaking out when Charlie reveals herself to be Lucifer's daughter, wherein he lets a cuss word slip in surprise.

He may be a little absent-minded or he just doesn't pay much close attention to some things, as he doesn't recognize Charlie's last name "Morningstar" to be the same "Morningstar" in Lucifer's name, making him unable to make a conclusion that she is Lucifer's daughter until Charlie told him.
ADVERTISEMENT

Abilities

Flight - As an Angel, he has wings that are capable of flight.
Gatekeeper - As the gatekeeper of heaven, he holds a vital role in granting entry to those seeking passage into heaven, ensuring that only deserving souls are admitted while safeguarding against any undesirable elements or discrepancies.
Skillset

Musical talent - He is adept at singing.
History

Past

Nothing is known about Peter's past except that at some point he would be given the title of "Saint" and became the Gatekeeper of Heaven.

Hazbin Hotel Season 1

"Welcome to Heaven"

Outside the gates of Heaven, St. Peter is standing with a large golden book of names to check who is permitted to enter Heaven.

When Charlie and Vaggie arrives Peter asks their names, and when Charlie answers he checks his book but is unable to find her name. After Charlie explains that her dad got her the meeting, Peter becomes incredibly shocked at the mention of Lucifer Morningstar, then asked if they were supposed to be there. Sera and Emily arrive and take over for Peter, and then Peter welcomes Charlie and Vaggie to Heaven and the trio of angels show them around.

ADVERTISEMENT
Gallery

St. Peter/Gallery
Trivia

St. Peter is based on the character of St. Peter from the first century depicted in the Bible.[1]
St. Peter in the Bible was one the Twelve Apostles of Jesus Christ, as well as the first Pope, and later the Gatekeeper of Heaven upon his death. St. Peter in Hazbin Hotel also appears to be the Gatekeeper of Heaven, but it is unknown if he was previously human.
Most depictions of St. Peter as guardian of Heaven's gates are of an old man with a beard; in Hazbin Hotel, Peter is portrayed as much younger looking.
St. Peter's yellow and blue garment in Hazbin Hotel is a reference to how the biblical figure is often depicted wearing yellow and blue clothing in paintings. A Christian Cross can also be seen at the bottom of St. Peter's garment.
According to the Hazbin Hotel Playbill page posted on Vivziepop's Instagram, St. Peter is the lead singer in Heavens royal choir as well as the founder of the Angelic drama club. He is also an accomplished harp and French horn player in what he calls the "Sera-ymphany orchestra

Tom Trench is a sinner demon and co-anchorman at 666 News. He is a supporting character in Hazbin Hotel who made his debut alongside his co-anchorman, Katie Killjoy, in the pilot.

Appearance

Tom is a demon with the face and neck being that of an expressive gas mask and light blonde sweeped-hair with paler streaks.

He is seen wearing a grey suit with slight darker-colored lapels, worn over a white collared shirt with a red necktie. He also has a red pocket square, and on his hands it appears to be covered with dark gray gloves.
Personality

Tom appears to have somewhat of a perverted personality, as he frequently makes sexual comments while covering stories on 666 News. He also appears to be neutral with Katie Killjoys's mean-spirited nature, and even participates in the mockery of Charlie after the reveal of Angel Dust's participation in the turf war and the subsequent undermining of Charlie's presentation of her project.

Despite this, it is implied that Tom is nicer than his co-host, as he looked ashamed when she kept making fun of Charlie.
Abilities

Immortality - As a Sinner, Tom is biologically immortal, being unable to die from illnesses and unable to age, remaining the same age as when he died, thus can not die of old age and other natural causes. He also cannot die from any kind of damage to the body, and will recover from any injury, however, he can only be permanently killed with angelic weaponry.
History

Past

Tom died in his 40s roughly during the time of World War 1, and once in Hell became a presenter of 666 News.

Hazbin Hotel pilot

After announcing the turf wars, involving Sir Pentious and Cherri Bomb, Katie pours hot coffee on Tom's crotch. When Charlie mentions her first client of the Happy Hotel is Angel Dust, Tom recognizes him as the porn star. As Charlie insulted Katie, Tom ran off set, and as the two women fought, Tom was set ablaze and screaming why nobody was helping him.

Hazbin Hotel Season 1

"Overture"

Katie Killjoy and Tom Trench report the breaking news that the Heaven Embassy has announced the new Extermination deadline to be six months instead of a year, and when Tom asks Katie what it means she replies that they're all royally fucked.

"The Show Must Go On"

When about to introduce himself, Katie Killjoy shoves Tom Trench out of his seat, saying no one cares who he is. When he returned to his seat his face was covered by a small screen, with him reacting by flipping his middle fingers up, much to his dismay.

Gallery

Tom Trench/Gallery
Trivia

His last name, Trench, refers to excavations dug in the ground used for military defense purposes.
When asked about what is behind Tom's gas mask, Vivziepop has stated, as far as she knows, his gas mask is simply his face.[4]
During a livestream where a viewer asked when each of the characters from the pilot had died, Vivziepop asked what year World War I had happened in. A person off-screen answered "the 1920s", to which Vivziepop reacted to with approval.[1] However, World War I lasted from 1914 to 1918, making the statement and his actual death date dubious.

Travis is a demon and a minor character in Hazbin Hotel, who also made a cameo appearance in the Helluva Boss episode "Spring Broken".

He is a regular patron of Angel Dust's, and is also shown to be a porn film director for him in "Masquerade".

Appearance

Travis is a demon of the avian variety, with owl-like "ears", facial disc, and short, pointy beak. His face is to be a lighter shade of gray, with his left eye having a black sclera with a red iris in the shape of a heart. He also has dark gray feathers all over his body and black claws for fingers.

He wears a trench coat the same shade of grey as his body which has feathered ends of his sleeves and at the bottom. He also wears a black trilby with a gray stripe.
Personality

Travis is a sleazy and crude demon who seems to dislike not having the last word. He is quick to sulk when people return his insults. He is portrayed as hypocritical and disrespectful, happily soliciting Angel's services while married, but still looking down on his profession, gleefully throwing targeted insults his way.

Travis makes a short appearance in the ADDICT music video during Angel Dust's pole dance, where he watches amorously by the side of the stage when Angel passes him.

Travis has been described by Vivziepop as "a whole mess".[1]
History

Hazbin Hotel pilot

After Angel Dust gave Travis a "fun time" in his car, Travis ran over a newly descended sinner and dropped Angel Dust off. When he called Angel a slut, he insulted Travis and gave him a kiss. Travis, irritated, drives off and a crash can be heard.

Hazbin Hotel Season 1

"Overture"

Whilst Charlie is singing and riding on the back of a Helluva Post van, Travis is drooling watching a television at a storefront window.

"Masquerade"

Seated beside Valentino during filming of Angel Dust, Travis is the director for the porno, but when Angel complains about the script, Travis appears annoyed, however, shakes his head nervously in agreement when Valentino asks if anyone watches for the dialogue. While Valentino and Angel Dust are in Angel's dressing room, Travis talks with the boom mic operator.

During Angel's performance, Travis can be seen watching the filming through a monitor nearby, and continues directing throughout.

"Dad Beat Dad"

While Alastor sings in competition with Lucifer, Travis is one of the silhouettes shown when Alastor sings "your steadfast hotelier".

Helluva Boss Season 1

"Spring Broken"

When Blitzo puts up a flyer for a 50% discount of I.M.P services during Earth's spring break, Travis is among the demons lining up for it.

Gallery

Travis/Gallery
Trivia

When requested to draw Travis holding a body pillow, Vivziepop mentioned the pillow being of "probably Angel Dust" before settling on Hatsune Miku, and further saying she thinks Travis would be very bisexual and that he likes "the anime girls and the Angel Dust".[2]
As shown in the ADDICT music video, Travis also watches Angel Dust perform, possibly implying he is a regular patron of Angel Dust's.
Travis wears a trilby, a felt hat that was popular in the 1920s with regular horse racing. This may suggest that Travis arrived in Hell during this time, if he was formerly human.
Travis is the only Hazbin Hotel character to make a physical cameo in Helluva Boss.
He shares the same voice actor as Cletus, Wally Wackford, and Mister Butler, with the four being voiced by Broadway actor and singer Don Darryl Rivera, who previously provided the singing voice for the character Jackson Wells on another of Vivziepop's projects, Zoophobia.
Travis is the only character whose voice actor reprised their role from the Hazbin Hotel pilot

Valentino is a tall, slender, somewhat muscular and broad-shouldered moth demon with lavender skin and lacking pupils and irises in his cerise-pink eyes, over which he is always depicted wearing gold-rimmed, heart-shaped sunglasses with cerise lenses.

His mouth is full of sharp, cerise teeth with a single golden fang that sits to his far left of center, a feature he shares with some of his employees like Angel Dust. He also has a long cerise tongue.

Valentino's stature is tall, estimated to be around 10 feet,[note 3] which he emphasizes with long black heeled boots. He has fluffy white neck fur with small red love-hearts that plumes up from his coat's break-line. He is bald[note 4] with moth-like antennae; the right appearing like a large white with black heart-striped feather while the left appears smaller and lacking the white areas.

He has an extra set of arms just above his hips. His hands and forearms are black, mimicking black gloves, while the upper halves are his normal skin color.

He has a pair of large red moth wings that features zebra print fur outlining the edges, while the interior is darker colored with several heart designs. These wings are usually wrapped around his body to form a floor-length coat with white fur at the wrists, as well as black-and-white-striped fur trim down the center-front to the bottom hem, and three white stripes on both hips with a heart shaped design on the back. This coat is pinned with a gold chain and gold love-heart shaped broach fastening at the breast.

He also has heart-shaped nipples colored in a darker shade of his skin tone, with gold piercings and a chain hung from them.

Valentino wears a red top hat with a wide, asymmetrical zebra-printed hat-band, in which his antennae poke out like feathers. Under his coat, he wears a chest-exposing dark grey shirt with rolled-up sleeves that are held together by two gold buttons, alongside white dress pants held by a black belt with a golden love-heart shaped buckle, and a pair of high-heeled black boots.

He wears a gold chain necklace hung down to his chest, gold arm bands on his lower wrists, each hand having one gold ring, and sometimes gold nail guards on his fingers.

According to Faustisse, Valentino wears fishnet stockings under his coat.[note 5] This is first seen in "Welcome to Heaven". In "The Show Must Go On", Valentino wears fishnet stockings, a black miniskirt, and black knee-high heeled boots.
Past

Valentino used to have both his antennae look identical, both like large white with black heart-striped feathers. He didn't have his sunglasses and gold fang, and his coat didn't have fur on the wrists and the outline wasn't fluffy. He wore a red fedora with a zebra print band, and white pants with a pink belt that had a gold heart-shaped buckle.

Pilot

In the pilot, Valentino's appearance was nearly the same, but with the exception of his right antennae being simply black-and-white striped and left antennae appearing more like a thorned-branch. His neck fur also had more red heart designs that are smaller, some of which being in two and some having a white area from the bottom of the heart.

His wing-coat lacked the white stripes in the back, as well as the brooch in the middle, while the black-and-white-striped fur trim down the center-front to the bottom hem had more stripes. His boots also appeared to have smaller heels.

ADVERTISEMENT

Personality

Valentino has been described as being charming[note 6] and roughly as level-headed as his fellow Overlord, Vox.[note 7] When he interacts with Charlie in his studio he acts cordial around her while struggling to hide his anger and irritation that he would prefer to take out on one of his employees instead, such as Angel Dust.

He does, eventually, show off his real behavior after some time. Valentino uses his charming persona in order to lure other demons into working for him, as shown in "Welcome to Heaven" where Valentino admitted spending much of his time in nightclubs, picking up demons and offering them "jobs" at his studios, with him hiding his more violent and psychotic behavior in order to convince them to willingly "work" for him.

Valentino is depicted as being controlling, abusive, and narcissistic, specifically towards one of his star employees, Angel Dust.[5][6] He also displays sadistic tendencies, appearing to take enjoyment in overriding Angel's consent, and remains seemingly unbothered by the trauma he is inflicting.

Valentino is frequently surrounded by a collection of the girls who work for him. He is ostentatious in displaying both his profession and status. Faustisse bluntly described him as "a huge fuckboi".[note 8] Despite this, he is apparently in a romantic relationship with Vox.

Valentino has been described by Angel to be a "psychopathic freak".[7] He has a reputation of throwing massive tantrums when one of his "whore" employees disobey him. Because of his temperamental side, he throws objects and rips other demons apart when he is angry, and he doesn't think about how his actions affect his and the Vees' image to where Vox had to explain that "chasing whores around town" will "fuck up" their "image". Once he calms down, he is more pragmatic and fully aware of possible negatives to acting too rashly.

On the other hand, even he has his limits. He was visibly shocked when Vox uncharacteristically snapped at him for wanting to murder everyone at the hotel. He is also terrified by Niffty's creepy stalker-ish and homicidal behavior.
ADVERTISEMENT

Abilities

Immortality - As a Sinner, Valentino is biologically immortal, being unable to die from illnesses and unable to age, remaining the same age as when he died, thus can not die of old age and other natural causes. He also cannot die from any kind of damage to the body, and will recover from any injury, however, he can only be permanently killed with angelic weaponry.
Strength - Valentino's strength appears to be greater than the average demon, being able to slam a door so hard a cupboard got knocked down "Masquerade", and was able to tear demons into pieces with his bare hands in "Radio Killed the Video Star", when Velvette recounts how he "tore up her best model", despite presumably not having any weapons on him. One display of his strength is when he ruthlessly physically abuses Angel Dust by choking him and slamming him around with a single hand.
Valentino using his wings to put out fire
Putting out a fire
Wings - Valentino has a pair of moth wings shown to be able to produce powerful gusts of wind that can easily put out a large fire with one flap.
Wing alteration - These wings can cover his body to form his coat, or can be hung down like a cape. It is possible his wings can form coats of various designs as he is seen in "Welcome to Heaven" wearing an alternate style coat.
Ocular, dental, and saliva illumination - Valentino's eyes give off a faint red glow, particularly if he's in a dark room, and his teeth can glow when he's giving a sinister smile. His red saliva also glows, mainly when he's acting perverted.
Multitasking - Valentino can multitask with his extra set of arms, such as holding his drink while he's decorating one of his guns.
Val Smoke
Valentino's red smoke
Typhokinesis - In the ADDICT music video, Valentino exhales a red, heart-shaped smoke from his cigarettes that has the ability to twist and form different shapes, entering the bodies of other demons, as Valentino directs it. However, a similar smoke is also present in a cigarette Angel smokes indicating that this is both from a specific cigarette he own and also a natural ability of Valentino, since, in "Masquerade," he smokes a cigarette Angel was smoking and the color of the smoke changes when he blows it into Angel's face.
Smoke constructs - Valentino can manipulate his red smoke into specific shapes that are physically solid, as shown in "Masquerade" where he formed a chain and manacles to bind Angel Dust and show his dominance over him.
Skillset

Weapon proficiency - As shown in the prequel comic, Valentino is easily able to shoot a moving target with accuracy from a notable distance away.
Charisma - Valentino possesses a flamboyant and vivacious charm that allows him to persuade others of his authority.[note 6]
Bilingualism - Valentino can fluently speak Spanish and English.
Angel Dust's contract
Valentino's contract with Angel Dust
Contracts - Like all Overlords, Valentino amassed his power and influence by "owning" souls. The method he uses to accomplish this is by having his victims sign their souls away to his ownership through the contracts he conjures, as shown in his ownership of Angel Dust, where the latter had willingly signed his real name in his contract to "work" for Valentino. However, in some cases, there are loopholes that makes them untouchable under certain circumstances, such as Angel being free from him and his influence outside his studio, which Valentino apparently can't remove. It is possible for Valentino to willingly render the contract null and void and release Angel from his control if he chooses to do so.
Artistic talent - It has been confirmed that Valentino is actually a talented artist.[8][9]
Singing and dancing - Valentino has shown to be a good singer and exceptional dancer, being able to performing a duet and dance with Vox.

Guns and pistols - Valentino has a collection of guns, such as a pink and zebra print revolver called "Moneyshot",[10] and a gold and black half pistol. He sometimes decorates them with glue, gemstones, and glitter, such as when he added "Valentino" to Moneyshot in "Radio Killed the Video Star".
ADVERTISEMENT

Gallery

Valentino/Gallery
Trivia

Valentino is an Italian name, meaning "brave or strong". It can also mean "a ladies' man", which is fitting considering his status as a pimp. It is likely also a reference to the word "valentine", which is near synonymous with love in many places.
According to Vivziepop the name "Valentino" came from her family's pet cat[11] who was put down in August 15, 2016, because he was suffering and old.[12] Vivziepop explained that the name was something she really loved and always wanted to name a character with, and thought it fit the character Valentino because it is a "very fancy name" that sounds "vaguely Latin", and also makes her think of Valentine's stuff.[11]
According to Sam Miller, background artist and art director of SpindleHorse, Valentino was Hispanic when living.[13]
Faustisse thinks that Valentino may have died in the 1970s.[note 9]
Dia and Summer in ADDICT 7
Valentino with Summer and Dia
When asked about Valentino's sexuality, Faustisse replied, "full pansexual".[note 2]
Vivziepop thinks that Valentino would be the kind of person to have a collection of canes.[14]
According to Vivziepop in a tweet, Valentino wishes he could visit the Lust Ring.[15]
As shown in "Radio Killed the Video Star" Valentino owns a customized Robo Fizz that he calls "Kitty".
Sometimes while Valentino speaks, he makes squeaking sounds like a moth.[16]
He sometimes switches between an American and a Hispanic accent when he is in the middle of a mood swing.
According to Angel Dust, Valentino's eyesight is so bad that he once spent a half hour counting a "stack" of bills, unaware there were only three in his hand. This is in reference to him looking at three bills in the ADDICT music video.[17]
According to Vivziepop, Valentino counting three bills in the ADDICT music video was something that slipped through the cracks in animation from the boards to final and he was supposed to be counting a stack of bills.[17]
The fur collar around Valentino's neck is an actual part of his body. This was previously implied in some of Valentino's now-deleted Voxtagram posts,[18] while this was officially confirmed in "Masquerade". He can feel from his collar, as shown in "Welcome to Heaven" when Niffty rips some fluff off for her collection he screams in pain.
Within the characters' Voxtagram accounts, Valentino was depicted in a romantic on-again off-again relationship with fellow Vees member, Vox. One that appeared, at times, to be verbally, physically, and psychologically abusive on his end.[19] Whether this relationship is reflective of their canon dynamic at all is currently unknown, as the actual events of the Instagram story arcs themselves are not.
In "The Show Must Go On", the two were dancing in a provocative and romantic nature, along with making out at the end implies they are dating.
Valentino was depicted in his Voxtagram posts as owning a creature named Queef, which he kept as a pet before killing it with a gun for annoying him.
His saliva is cerise pink like his eyes and tongue.
Prior to the series' release, Faustisse was not of the opinion that Valentino cares about Angel Dust being at the Hazbin Hotel.[note 10] This however is not canon in the series as shown in the episode "Radio Killed the Video Star" Valentino was greatly enraged that Angel started living at the Hotel.
As revealed in "Welcome to Heaven", while the exact details are unknown, according to the contract Angel Dust has signed that gave Valentino ownership of his soul, Valentino can only "Do whatever he wants" to Angel within his porn studio, giving Angel some measure of freedom when he is outside of it. Given that Angel formerly lived in the studio with Valentino, this can possibly be the real reason to Valentino's anger of the former moving into the Hazbin Hotel, as this allowed Angel to escape Valentino's full control.
Valentino's Logo
Valentino's symbol in the series
Valentino's symbol was made by Sam Miller and is an elevated design of the one she made for the ADDICT music video; it has a subtle XXX within a moth design, and somewhat resembles a skull.[20]
Judging by the numerous posters of Valentino posing nearly naked with his guns, it is possible Valentino may have partaken in some form of acting himself.
According to Vivziepop, finding a voice actor for Valentino was the hardest of the cast, as there was a lot of amazing auditions but everyone locked into exactly what was written on the audition sheet and none of them were really clicking with her. She also had offered the role to other actors, who all declined, so after she had asked Andrew Butler if he could bring in anyone to do parts in Helluva Boss and he brought in Joel Perez, Vivziepop immediately liked Joel's energy and thought he would have a good shot at Valentino, so she asked him to read for it and immediately thought he was perfect.[21]
Development

Valentino was a very late addition in the development of Hazbin Hotel, with Faustisse noting that the character was still being worked on, even past the release of the pilot.[note 11]
Joel Perez explained that originally in the script for Season 1, Valentino did not speak Spanish and did not have an accent. He explained that after he did two takes in completely unaccented English for the first scene he recorded, where Valentino was trashing the place after finding Angel Dust had left, Vivziepop asked Joel to do an improvised take on the scene with how he himself would be when angry and Joel started peppering in Spanish, which Vivziepop liked and decided to have Joel pepper in-and-out and continue doing so while developing the show.[22][23]

"We know not how this perished. Mayhaps 'twas not by a demon's hand at all. If we rush to war without knowing, mightn't they purge all of Hell for daring an uprising?"
―Zestial, to Velvette regarding the proposal on fighting against Heaven
Zestial is a demon and one of the many powerful Overlords of Hell, as well as the oldest living Overlord in power.[2][1] He made a cameo in the pilot and his official debut in "Scrambled Eggs".


ADVERTISEMENT
Appearance

Zestial is a lanky, spider-like demon with dark gray skin and four lime green eyes. He wears all-black clothing, with a pitch black cloak that covers most of his body. When Zestial unfurls his cloak, his eyes glow and the top pair gain red irises.

At the front of his cloak is a large black spider with lime green stripes on its eight legs, as well as lime green eyes and lime green on its back. The interior of his cloak is lime green with a spider web pattern and four red spider legs extending across the cloak.

He also wears a distinctive big black top hat with a light grey patch at the front, along with a gray skull and a lime green-and-maroon-striped feather on the right side.
Personality

Zestial speaks in an archaic dialect redolent of early modern English. He has a very sophisticated way of speaking, and often keeps his temper rather than get easily frustrated, as the case when Velvette mocks him. However, despite his overall demeanor, he can be slightly petty, loudly sipping his tea to cut Velvette off mid-sentence before opposing her proposal to fight back against the Exorcists.

His reputation is such that demons other than his fellow Overlords are terrified of him, hiding or cowering whenever he passes by. The sight of him causes one civilian to set himself on fire out of fear.

Befitting his advanced age, Zestial is extremely patient and cautious, telling Velvette that they shouldn't take immediate action in spite of being given proof that Exorcists can be killed out of fear of the potential repercussions.

He is also shown to be compassionate to those with which he is close, sensing Carmilla's tension after an Overlord meeting and offering her an ear upon which to vent her concerns.

However, he has also demonstrated a more sadistic side to himself, stating that he "revels in the screams" while talking with Alastor about the potential for acid rain in the afternoon.
ADVERTISEMENT

Abilities

Demon transformation - He can change into a stronger demon form.
Conjuration - Zestial is seemingly able to create objects out of thin air, doing so to produce a full cup of tea and plate during the Overlord meeting.
Bioluminescent generation - Zestial's eyes, and parts of his spider accessory, can glow when he unfurls his cloak.
Skillset

Musical talent - He is adept in singing.
Intelligence - Presumably due to his age and how long he has spent in Hell he has vast intellectual ability. This was demonstrated during his opposing statements against Velvette's proposal to enter war against the Exorcists, because despite evidence an exorcist was killed they do not know how it was killed, explaining that if they go to war without any information on how to kill Angels then they would destroy all of Hell for rebelling. He, along with Velvette, eventually deduced that Carmilla was responsible for the Angels death due to how she was acting during the meeting, making him confront her about it in private and comfort her.
ADVERTISEMENT
History

Past

Nothing is currently known about Zestial's past except that he is known to be the oldest Overlord in Hell,[2] referred to as "ancient" by Alastor.[3] He has earned a feared reputation, with the mere sight of him causing demons to flee in terror or cause self destruction just to avoid him.

Hazbin Hotel pilot

After the recent Extermination, Zestial is seen in a room that he hid in with Carmilla Carmine and Zeezi, alongside Lucifer Morningstar.

A demon trying to steal from Zestial
A demon trying to steal from Zestial
While Charlie is singing during her interview at 666 News, she momentarily appears beside a demon who is attempting to steal bread from Zestial until Zestial unfurls his cloak and terrifies the demon.

Later when Vaggie explains to Angel Dust about Alastor's origins, several overlords can be seen, including Zestial.

Hazbin Hotel Season 1

"Scrambled Eggs"

He approaches Alastor and the Egg Boiz on a street and says that it has been years since he had seen Alastor. Throughout their walk, demons who saw Zestial would run away or harm themselves out of fear. He and Alastor walked to Carmilla's building for a meeting with several other Overlords.

We can't act without more intelligence
Zestial telling Velvette they can't act without more intelligence
In the meeting when Velvette presented a deceased Exorcist's head and proposed to fight back against the angels in the next Extermination, Zestial commented that they should not act without further intelligence on the matter. Velvette began insulting Zestial, but Carmilla came to his defense, scolding her for her disrespect.

After Carmilla ended the meeting, Zestial followed Carmilla and her daughters to her office to talk to her and suspected Carmilla to be the one who killed the Angel, since he says that being angry isn't like her. He further comforts her on the matter, encouraging her to talk about it.

ADVERTISEMENT

Relationships

Fellow Overlords

Alastor

Alastor is seemingly on friendly terms with Zestial, and was shown to have respect for Hell's oldest Overlord. It's also noteworthy that Zestial is one of the only male characters Alastor doesn't act hostile or disrespectful towards.

In "Scrambled Eggs", Alastor greets Zestial during a walk with the Egg Boiz to Carmilla's building for a meeting. Alastor quickly told the Egg Boiz to be quiet, and remained cordial with Zestial during the walk. Zestial was interested in Alastor's 7-year absence, and while Alastor says that his absence wasn't anything serious, he was interested to hear the theories about what they think happened. At the meeting, Alastor agreed with Zestial's stance of not going to war with the exorcists without further intel on how to kill them.

Carmilla Carmine

Carmilla defends Zestial's honor when Velvette is rude to him, showing that the two have a good relationship. As stated by Carmilla, Zestial and Carmilla have known each other for a long time and have been friends and as well as allies as Overlords. As demonstrated when Zestial was also able to tell that something was bothering Carmilla and offered to hear her out to help get it off her chest. This closeness was also shown when Zestial easily deduced that Carmilla was the one responsible for killing the Exorcist that Velvette had brought to their meeting, based on her reaction to the head being brought to their meeting.

According to the Hazbin Hotel Playbill page posted on Vivziepop's Instagram, Zestial is currently assisting Carmilla with her endeavors due to them being on friendly terms and having similar mindsets.[1]

Velvette

At the meeting, when Velvette brought a deceased Exorcist's head and proposed to fight back, he viewed Velvette as foolish, stating that they should not act without knowing how the angel had died. He remains calm but irritated when she insults him.

ADVERTISEMENT

Gallery

Zestial/Gallery
Trivia

According to the "Clocktower Countdown to Premiere" livestream, Zestial is the oldest Overlord in Hell,[2] with Alastor referring to him as "ancient" and Velvette insulting him with "grandpa", "old man", "fossil", and "senile" in the show itself. However, whether he is the oldest by age or by how long he has reigned is unclear.
The Hazbin Hotel Playbill page posted on Vivziepop's Instagram specifies that Zestial is the "oldest living Overlord in power".[1]
According to the Hazbin Hotel Playbill page posted on Vivziepop's Instagram, Zestial was once one of the most feared Overlords, but is now effectively retired, spending his days roaming Hell and enjoying the spoils, and currently assisting Carmilla with her endeavors.[1]
He shares the same voice actor as Vortex and Asmodeus in Helluva Boss, being voiced by James Monroe Iglehart.

"Welcome, Hell's sovereign Overlords. I've invited you all here because you represent the controlling powers of our city. Together, you own millions of souls. Souls that are at risk with the new Extermination schedule."
―Carmilla Carmine, to her fellow Overlords at their meeting
Overlords are a class of powerful Demons in Hell. They rank just above regular Sinner Demons and place fifth in terms of power in Hell's hierarchy.[1]

The concept of Overlords was first introduced in the pilot of Hazbin Hotel during the scene where Vaggie explains to Angel Dust about Alastor's origins.

Description

The Overlords rule over certain parts of Hell, each commanding a domain of influence to which Sinner demons submit. Their estate varies from minor to major, as does their reputation, with some being so infamous that lesser beings have been seen cowering at the mere sight of a prominent Overlord in the street. Even demons who have more power and strength than said Overlord, like Charlie, can be fearful. Power struggles between Overlords give rise to both alliances and rivalries, such as the alliance of the Vees or the rivalries between Alastor and Vox or Carmilla and Velvette.

As stated by Carmilla Carmine, Overlords gain and increase their power by owning souls. A small group of overlords can collectively own millions of the souls that reside in Hell and exploit them to increase their own power and influence. Ownership can be direct, such as by having a victim sign away their soul through a contract or by striking a soul-binding deal. Valentino's binding of Angel Dust is accomplished through such a contract, and Alastor's bargain-struck possession of Husk is similarly unbreakable. The binding power of deals was later confirmed in "Hello Rosie!", where Alastor sealed a deal with Charlie via handshake and verbal agreement. Deals need not involve a soul, but always follow a stated term of exchange.[2]

There could be loopholes that can be found in an Overlord's contract or deal, such as with Angel Dust: while Valentino owns his soul, he can physically exploit Angel Dust only while they are in his studio. Valentino is never seen teleporting his debtors to himself despite having ample motive, unlike Alastor who can summon Husk, as well as some demons to fix the hotel wall in "Radio Killed the Video Star", at his will. In "The Show Must Go On", Alastor himself is revealed to be seeking his freedom by looking for a way out of his own deal.

Some Overlords may also form affiliations with each other to create alliances that differ in scope. One such alliance is between Vox, Valentino, and Velvette, who are joined in a special Overlord triumvirate called the "Vees" as major influencers in the media industry.[3][4] In "Hello Rosie!", Alastor and Rosie are shown to have some kind of alliance as Rosie offers Alastor some opportune real estate to make some deals, and she agrees to his asking for help in protecting the Hazbin Hotel.

Though some Overlords are condemned to remain in the Pride Ring due to their origins as Sinner demons, their influence can extend beyond the Pride Ring, such as Carmilla's weapons and Vox's merchandise that can be found in the other rings of Hell. Further, Carmilla Carmine gained the reputation as the "top weapons dealer" in Hell, suggesting that their businesses, names, and reputation can spread to the other rings of Hell.

An Overlord can lose their status by loss of influence or by unfavorable bargain, even selling their own soul. In "Masquerade", Husk reveals that he was once an overlord before betting his soul in a gamble to keep his power. An Overlord might alternatively keep their status and influence even if deal-bound, as shown by Alastor who is in a deal with another.
Cultural Relations

Some Overlords don't get along with each other either due to personal relations or disagreement with practices. One example is the rivalry between Vox and Alastor, whom have different views on technology and the latter refusing the former's offer to join his team.

Some lower-ranked demons look up to Overlords, like Sir Pentious who idolized the Vees and wanted to join them, while others wish to kill Overlords, such as Striker who offered Blitzo to join him in slaying Overlords. In addition, some demons dislike Overlords in general, and due to little consequence for having no respect for high-ranked demons, the only way to keep a demon passive to an Overlord is through fear and power.

Due to an Overlord possessing the ability to own a demons soul through deals and contracts, both parties of the deal can take advantage of their side, often exploiting it. One example is the deal between Angel Dust and Valentino; Valentino can do what he pleases to Angel while he is in the studio while Angel is free of him when he is outside of the studio. Additionally, the relationships between an Overlord and a soul they own can be overall negative, such as the case with Alastor and Husk, and Valentino and Angel.

Trivia

When asked if Stolas was a fellow Overlord, Vivziepop stated that he is part of a separate hierarchal ranking which she refers to as "the Goetia Demons".[5]
Some Overlords appear to represent a form of media. Examples of such cases being Alastor with radio, Vox with television, Valentino with pornography, Velvette with social media, and Carmilla Carmine and her daughters with ballet.
During the pilot episode scene where Vaggie explains Alastor's origins as an overlord, a collage of eleven demons is shown.
Also shown are silhouettes of both Husk and Niffty behind Alastor, suggesting the two were somehow tied to the Overlords. However, only Husk is revealed to be a former Overlord, while Niffty is known only to be Alastor's associate.
Later, the demons Bethesda and Frederick, who were not shown in the collage, are confirmed to be Overlords.[note 1]
According to Faustisse, Alastor has no interest in being an Overlord since power is not what he really desires.[note 2] Despite this, he is still regarded as an Overlord by technicality.
However, this detail may not be canon to the series anymore, as Alastor attended the Overlord meeting at Carmilla's building in "Scrambled Eggs". This could possibly indicate that while he may not desire power, he is willing to have a position as an Overlord anyway.
In the unofficial Voxtagram stories, Vox, Valentino, and Velvette were originally called the VVV Overlords.[6] In these stories, the group regularly hung out together, where Velvette seemed to be the glue that binds the other two together. A 2022 teaser for the main series revealed that the trio's official name is the "Vees".[3]
BetaDramaOverlord
Early version of an Overlord
During an early version of the Hazbin Hotel pilot scene that depicts various overlords there was an overlord whose design originally had a single, more owl-like face and wore a hat, but in the final version was changed to have two faces and lacked the hat.[7]
Another change in the final version was the inclusion of Velvette, whose placement covers another Overlord with a pair of curled horns. This Overlord can still be slightly seen in the final version.[7]
In "The Harvest Moon Festival", Striker mentions in his pitch to Blitzo that instead of working for sinners he "could be slaying Overlords" and "could partner up with [Striker] and kill...the unkillable", which may imply Striker has killed or has the means to kill Overlords.
Overlords can lose their status, such as Husk who in "Masquerade" mentioned once being an Overlord before losing everything from gambling, especially to Alastor.
Zestial is the oldest of the Overlords, while Velvette is the youngest,[8] although it is unclear if this refers to their biological age or length of time as Overlords.
It is unknown if becoming an Overlord is limited to Sinners or if hellborn demons can also be Overlords.
Frederick and Bethesda are both hellborn demons, which supports the possibility that any demon of a certain background can acquire the rank.
When talking about the themes of Hazbin Hotel in a 2024 video, Vivziepop mentions that "Overlords are Sinners who gained power", possibly implying that most, if not all, Overlords are Sinners.[9]
Rockstar Bird Overlord
Vassago's appearance in the Hazbin Hotel pilot
Prior to his appearance in Helluva Boss, Vassago first appeared in the pilot episode of Hazbin Hotel, where he was seen among the Overlords in Vaggie's story, implying he was part of the ranking. It is unknown if his status as an Overlord will be carried over into the main series and its spin-off.
The large dinosaur-looking Overlord first seen in the Hazbin Hotel pilot, is confirmed to be named Zeezi from closed captions in "Scrambled Eggs".
As shown with Valentino and Angel Dust in "Masquerade", and Alastor with Husk in "Dad Beat Dad", Overlords can manifest their ownership and dominance over the demons whose soul they own via chains, collars, and manacles they can conjure with their powers.

"Well, hello there, you wayward Sinner. Do you like blood, violence, and depravity of a sexual nature? Of course you do! That's why you're in Hell. But what would you say if I told you there was a place to stay that had none of that? Welcome to the Hazbin Hotel, a misguided path to redemption! Founded five days ago by Lucifer's delusional daughter, Charlotte Morningstar! Come place your fate in her inexperienced hands as she tries to work through her daddy issues by fixing you!"
―Alastor, in his Hazbin Hotel commercial

The Hazbin Hotel, formerly known as the Happy Hotel, is a hotel run by Charlie Morningstar for clients who are undergoing rehabilitation to stay at. It is located in Pentagram City within the Pride Ring of Hell.[2]

Description

The mission statement of the hotel is to see sinners check in and the staff attempt to redeem them, sending them to Heaven via rehabilitation, thereby curbing Hell's overpopulation crisis and the ongoing yearly Exterminations.

The hotel suffers ongoing mockery and criticism from most of Hell's denizens, most notably the 666 News anchor Katie Killjoy, who deems the idea of reforming demons laughable.
History

The Hazbin Hotel was previously owned by the royal family before being abandoned for unknown reasons. The hotel formerly may have served as a mansion of sorts while it was owned and inhabited by the family prior to its transformation into a hotel, as suggested by the prevalence of pictures of Charlie, family, and friends on the walls of the establishment.

At some point prior to the events of the Dirty Healings comic and pilot, Charlie assumed ownership of the structure and began to repurpose it towards being a hotel aimed at redeeming sinners. Charlie was subsequently successful in enticing a single sinner, Angel Dust, to inhabit the hotel as its first client, albeit being done under financial incentive.

In the Hazbin Hotel pilot following a disastrous interview with 666 News, Alastor approached the hotel and offered his services as a business partner to promote the hotel, though only with the intention of watching sinners try and fail to redeem themselves. Charlie accepts this offer, as she welcomes any and all the help she could get. Alastor subsequently altered the name of the hotel from the "Happy Hotel" to the "Hazbin Hotel".

In "The Show Must Go On", the hotel was destroyed by Adam during the early Extermination. It was promptly rebuilt after the battle by the hotel group and Lucifer, who made the building much larger than before.

Exterior

The Hazbin Hotel exterior was a tall, elaborate amalgamation of arched windows and turrets, one of which seems to be broken. In the pilot, the building's exterior suffered from being in a state of extreme disrepair and untidiness.

It appears to be at least seven stories tall, with at least five of which being guest floors. Remnants of an airship, an ocean liner, a sailing ship and a carousel litter both sides and appear to have been incorporated into the structure of the building itself; there is also a train with some tracks looping the first and second floor exterior. Located on the top right of the building is a small radio broadcasting room, used as the work area for Alastor.

Many signs are displayed outside the hotel: One atop the entrance reminiscent of the Hazbin Hotel logo, a large pink one atop the building with the hotel's name in lights, a neon 'HOTEL' sign at the bottom right and atop the building where Alastor's broadcast room is located, a small 'On-Air' sign is visible. Also located on the outer facade are various arrows pointing to the entrance and the broadcast room.

The entrance has a tented cover with a booth in the center reminiscent of a circus or theater ticket booth. On either side of the booth are a set of double doors that have stained glass; in the pilot, they depicted an apple on each one but were destroyed by an explosion due to Sir Pentious blowing up the doors with his airship.

At the end of the pilot, the sign name is changed from the "Happy Hotel" to "Hazbin Hotel" by Alastor.

Interior

The hotel's interior was shown to be in a state of disrepair, with wooden boards covering shattered windows, signs warning of asbestos, bloodied tools left lying around, and paintings are shown hanging off the walls. Much of the furniture in the lobby are strewn around haphazardly or remain boxed up in several large wooden crates. In the pilot, the building's interior suffered from being in a state of extreme disrepair and untidiness.

The bar uses skeletons, snakes, and bones as general themes, along with card suits and candles, and advertises itself as a casino. The area the bar in has glowing green wooden walls instead of the usual red wallpaper, with a "Jackpot" sign on the left wall and a Beelzejuice neon sign on the right wall. The word "concierge" can be presumed to be shown above the bar, and Alastor calls it the front desk when talking to Husk, suggesting that it is also the check-in counter.

Despite the shabby and poor condition of the hotel, the overall theme of the building remains ornate and regal, with stained glass windows, lavish furniture, and generous usage of gold. Like the rest of Hell, the hotel has a largely red color scheme. There are many apple, snake and circus motifs throughout the hotel's interior, in reference to the royal family, or more specifically, Lucifer Morningstar. Eyes are also a recurring theme throughout the building, appearing on the frame of almost every single painting and several vases and jars.

Charlie and Vaggie's room

The room the two women shared was rather large, with a regal look and a large bed, and has a window with a view of Pentagram City.

Angel Dust's room

In the ADDICT music video, Angel's room had striped wallpaper with spider patterns, a vanity, mirrors, a place to put his wigs, and a bed. In "Radio Killed the Video Star", his wallpaper lacks the spider patterns, and his bed has several pillows of various design, while beside it is a small bed for Fat Nuggets shaped like a pink heart with a small pillow on top, and with both beds on a single platform with neon lights. The wall behind the bed has photos of him, Cherri, and Fat Nuggets, as well as a couple of his film posters, while the bedside wall has neon lights shaped like webs.

In "The Show Must Go On", the door to his room is shown to have neon lights shaped like webs with hearts, and has three photos of him and his friends, and Fat Nuggets.

Alastor's room

Alastor's room has a mixture between both traditional décor and the fantastical, with one half being a classic "fancy study", complete with tasteful wallpaper and furnishings, the other half being a literal swamp conjured as a dining area.

Sir Pentious' room

Sir Pentious' room shares his airship's steampunk aesthetics of golden cogs and gears and a red and black color scheme. His bed is shown to be a circular mattress lined with pillows.

Trivia

Both the Hotel redesign and the rebuilt Hotel main series designs were made by Sam Miller.[3][4]
The top of the rebuilt Hotel bears slight similarity in shape to the head, cobra-hood, and hat of Sir Pentious, most likely meant to memorialize him.
The prototype exterior of the hotel bears a striking resemblance to the Hotel Hightower located in the Tokyo DisneySea theme park resort in Urayasu, Japan.
By extension, the style of architecture used for the hotel's facade is known as Moorish Revival while the roofing style is known as Queen Anne style, which carried over in more articulation to the working design of the hotel.
The Hazbin Hotel may be similar to the idea of Purgatory in certain sects of Christianity, as both are methods of cleansing sin to bring dead souls to Heaven.
During the scene while Niffty is cleaning the hotel, a clock similar to the "Conditional Immortality" clock from the webcomic, Homestuck, is shown.
According to Sam Miller, the carpets of the hotel seen in the ADDICT music video have a pattern based on vintage circus tickets.[5]
According to Alastor in the Hotel's first commercial he made in "Overture", the Hotel still does not have a working phone.

Pentagram City, also referred to as The Pentagram, is one of the cities of Hell, being located in the Pride Ring. It is the primary setting of Hazbin Hotel.

Description

The Pentagram is the main city from Hell in which the series of Hazbin Hotel focuses on. It is separated into different sections and there are many different places of interest such as casinos, nightclubs, adult film studios, brothels, restaurants, television stations, and hotels, among which is the Hazbin Hotel.

Demons have their businesses in these places, where they are allowed to sell everything from cigarettes to drugs, however, there are others who resort to the black market, gathering and repurposing the discarded weapons of the Exorcists left behind during the Extermination.

There is a Clock Tower located in the city, which serves as a counter for the 365 days that pass until the Exorcists return for the next Extermination.

Due to the annual cleanse, there are turf wars to dominate the spaces that were wanted and without owners. Sir Pentious and Cherri Bomb are the two main turf fighters in the Hazbin Hotel pilot.

Cannibal Town is one of the towns of Pentagram City in Hell.

Description

The town's aesthetic resembles old Americana and an American town in the 1910s,[2] being filled with buildings that possess more vintage architecture. Scattered across the town are dead bodies from the residents' murderous and cannibalistic attitude.

Everything in the town fits this vintage theme from its automobiles all the way to the clothing its residents wear, which is why Alastor likes going there since it closely resembles the era he lived in back on Earth. He is additionally quite popular in the town, being a regular visitor with a vintage personality.

The inhabitants likewise share a friendly and old-fashioned demeanor, but as cannibals, they are incredibly violent. The only way to avoid their wrath is to adapt to their vintage attitude, as anyone who visits the place and looks like they're from a different era would subsequently be eaten by them.[1]

However, to their own kind they are kind to each other and the town itself is nice and orderly (especially by Hell's standards and to Charlie's surprise). Alastor attributes it all to Rosie's leadership. The residents stick together no matter what, even if someone isn't particularly well liked. As Rosie puts it: "If you want to convince any of them, you have to convince all of them".
History

In the Hazbin Hotel pilot, after the recent Extermination, Odette and another demon pass through Cannibal Town collecting Angelic Weapons while Rosie is seen crossing out the name "Franklin" from the emporium's sign since Franklin likely perished during the Extermination.

In "Overture", while Charlie sung about it being a Happy Day in Hell and grabbed a ride on a Helluva Post van that drove her past V Tower and into Cannibal Town where she got off and gets brains in her eye from one of the many corpses of Sinners being devoured by the residents and then headed toward the Heaven Embassy.

In "Hello Rosie!", after Alastor makes a deal with Charlie for information on the Exorcists, Alastor takes her to Cannibal Town to meet Rosie and to try gain allies for the upcoming fight against Adam. In Rosie's Emporium, Rosie is seen talking to a cannibal about their husband, saying she would straighten him out, while Charlie grabbed a souvenir. Rosie notices Alastor, and approaches Alastor and Charlie, and after introductions, Rosie asks why they are here, which when Alastor explains that they need help to fend off the Extermination, but while Rosie agrees to it she warns Charlie that she needs to convince all of them. In the town square while Charlie tries to gain the cannibals' support, a cannibal resident named Susan heckles her, causing Charlie to lose her temper. Rosie takes Charlie back into the emporium and asks about her troubles and about how she usually pitches her Hotel, and despite Charlie believing that singing never works, Rosie affirms that it will work here. Back outside, Charlie talks to the crowd again, this time rallying them through a song, and Charlie rallies the cannibals back to the Hotel.

Trivia

The town was originally called "Cannibal Colony" in the setting of The Radio Demon comic.
Cannibals
Cannibals with red eyes
In the pilot, all of the cannibals were shown to have red eyes rather than black, except for Rosie's.
The cannibal residents have a similar appearance of pale skin, black eyes, sharp teeth, and body shape, suggesting they may belong to the same species of demon.
In a late-2019 livestream, while Vivziepop explained that there are Sinners from throughout history who have survived the Exterminations in Hell, she brought up that the residents of Cannibal Town have become a cannibal colony because they are all from the 1910s, implying that some if not all the cannibals are sinners.[3] This is further evidenced by Charlie referring to only sinners when talking to the army of cannibals in "The Show Must Go On".[4]
In the The Radio Demon comic, the cannibals were shown with more variety in their appearance, such as some having irises or pupils, white eyes, and one shown having a single eye and a barb-tipped tail. This diversity in appearance seems to be absent outside of the comic.
According to Vivziepop, the residents of Cannibal Town are all really cliquey.[3]
The gimmick of the children in Cannibal Town is that they look really innocent and cute but they're all cannibals and like monsters
